# Before Christ: native port reference

The requested target is Side Arms Special's **Before Christ** program, with its
behavior preserved and a Genesis graphics remaster. It is a separate program
from both the CD's Standard mode and the existing arcade-derived Genesis game.

The art direction uses our existing Genesis robots, enemies, effects and
background artwork, with richer remastered colors. PC Engine graphics provide
animation and placement references. Replacement art must retain source gameplay
positions, collision dimensions and timing. P3/P4 remain recolors of the original
two robots. The current Vivid color mapping is already enabled by default;
additional simultaneous-color capacity has not been implemented. Color work
must stay within the actual renderer palette allocation and the requested
60 fps / 100% speed budget, including 3P and 4P.

**Status: all ten rounds run natively; full completion remains unverified.**
Normal, Before Christ and Boss Rush expose 1–4P selection modals. Continuous
assisted runs now clear all ten BC rounds at every player count through ordinary
combat, without forced boss defeats or round jumps. Continuous protected runs
also launch through the real Home player modal, complete the bonus/gallery/credits
and return to Home at every player count. Separate checks cover co-op controls/scaling.
The bonus, fades, twenty-entry gallery, credits, finite native music and
return/re-entry sequence pass native 1P/2P/3P/4P checks, including wrapped
bonuses and frozen complete party state. A 4P gallery stack/heap overlap was
found and fixed by the stronger checks described at the end of this document.

Natural full-campaign behavior, broader art/audio fidelity and sustained
60 fps / 100% speed remain unfinished. No whole-game 1:1 claim is made.
The sections below record work chronologically; later verified results
supersede earlier interim limitations.

## Source and observations

The user's CD archive and System Card BIOS are in Downloads. UnRAR successfully
extracted the complete archive; `tools/probe_pce_cd.py` checked all 4,792 MODE1
sectors. The 9,814,016-byte data track has SHA-256:

`4915e947782df7bbd10f2b46a615866400ab3a66ea49b6762d2497d540840364`

MAME 0.288 boots the supplied BIOS and CD, selects Before Christ, and starts it.
`tools/pce_oracle.py` / `tools/pce_capture.lua` capture screenshots, VRAM,
palette RAM, sprite attributes, work RAM, CPU banks, and code snapshots.
Local captures exist for the first 12,000 emulated frames of each of the ten
rounds, using debug invulnerability and one-hit bosses to inspect progression.
Those assisted captures are reference observations, not difficulty/playthrough
validation. Original ROMs, dumps and screenshots remain under ignored `.local/`.

The stage-select and debug addresses were initially located with the
[PCE cheat reference](https://wikiwiki.jp/tg002/%E3%82%B5%E3%82%A4%E3%83%89%E3%82%A2%E3%83%BC%E3%83%A0%E3%83%BB%E3%82%B9%E3%83%9A%E3%82%B7%E3%83%A3%E3%83%AB),
then checked against execution of the user's game. No cheats belong in the port.

## First native rules

`src/bc_rules.c` is native C suitable for the 68000; it does not interpret or
emulate HuC6280 instructions. The following CPU addresses refer to the observed
BC bank mapping: MPR2–6 = $80–$84, with the first CD RAM bank at CPU $4000.

| Source routine | Native rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| $8F39–$8F60; tables $9BC7/$9BE7 | Direction vector: axial speed 3, diagonal speed 2; speed-up gives 4/3. Conflicting directions give zero motion. | All 32 table cases match. |
| $808D–$8118 | Terrain uses 4096×4096 wrapped world coordinates, 32×32 metatiles in 256-pixel blocks, and four 16×16 collision subcells. | Used in the movement trace comparisons. |
| $8F39–$902E | Horizontal and vertical probes, scroll pushback, fixed-point movement and limits x=16..240, y=32..200. | 1,800 controllable movement frames match positions and velocities exactly, including terrain and boundary stops. |
| $90B8–$90EF; $9838–$988B | Held-fire counter, 64-update charge cap, facing, release/both-button handling and beam launch decision. | 2,700 consecutive charge frames match counters/latches/facing; seven observed launches match the number of segments. |

Charge releases below 40 updates produce no beam; 40–49 produce three segments,
50–59 four, and 60+ five. An occupied beam pool consumes the release without a
new beam. The first two normal projectile types are now ported as described below;
the option weapons and enemy damage paths are covered separately below. Charged-beam flight is now ported as described below. Charge sound command selection is transcribed from
the routine; audio equivalence has not been tested.

The tests compile the same native rules as a host library for differential
comparison with actual PCE captures. The SGDK/68000 build also compiles cleanly.
The rules are not yet called by the game's runtime, so this does not certify
the complete cartridge or its performance. Crush/death/entry transitions are
outside the current movement fixture; diagonal vectors are table-checked but
not yet exercised in that movement trace.

## Charged-beam flight

`bc_beam_launch` and `bc_beam_step` translate $9889–$99B9 and the beam's
$9A9F–$9B95 update path. Head, body and tail retain the original sprite IDs
as renderer-independent identifiers. Native code preserves staggered segment
acceleration, 16-pixel-per-update speed, four-update animation timers, left-facing
head/tail flips, 24-bit fixed-point coordinates, and retirement order. The
source's carry flag feeds its offscreen bound calculation; this is reproduced
explicitly instead of replacing it with a symmetric rectangle test.

`tools/qa_bc_beam.py` compares all active slot fields continuously against full
MAME work-RAM traces. Two fixtures passed, each exercising all three lengths in
both directions: 266 active slot updates and 24 retirements per fixture (532
updates and 48 retirements total). The second fixture initializes unused slot
fractions to 1/127/128/254/255 before tracing to test their preservation on reuse.
These reference-only RAM pokes do not belong in the cartridge. Launch placement,
velocity, counters, sprite IDs/attributes and retirement match exactly.

This is beam flight only: enemy damage, sound playback, rendered sprite artwork,
and mode integration are not covered. The rules still need to be connected to
the complete BC runtime; a clean 68000 compile is not an in-game performance test.

## Spread weapons (weapon IDs 0 and 1)

`bc_shot_fire` and `bc_shot_step` translate the straightening spread
($90FC–$9291) and expanding spread ($92AB–$9451). Both retain five power tiers,
the original descending volley order, a shared 28-slot allocation search,
reused fractional coordinates, fixed-point velocities, terrain probes,
animation timing and offscreen retirement. `bc_shot_hit` schedules an enemy
impact for the next projectile update; `bc_shot_impact` handles the impact
animation. This ordering was confirmed by a write at PC $A0BA after movement.

`tools/qa_bc_shots.py` continuously compares native slot fields with source RAM.
The five-tier/both-direction fixture passed 889 active updates / 60 retirements.
The rapid-fire fixture passed 8,169 updates / 521 retirements, with 11 volleys
limited by pool capacity and 128 expansion transitions. A separate round-2 cave
fixture passed 897 updates / 60 retirements, including three terrain impacts.
The first two fixtures had **no terrain impacts**; only the cave fixture validates
that branch. The cave also exposed relocated player routines (a $217-byte offset);
the verifier locates the update signature instead of assuming round-1 addresses.

Enemy collision notifications are explicitly replayed from the source's write
trace (10, 13 and 11 respectively). This tests the projectile's response to a
contact, **not native enemy overlap detection, HP, scoring or death behavior**.
These modules still are not wired into a playable BC runtime. Returning and option weapons are covered separately below.

Reproduce the cave comparison:

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/qa_bc_shots.py \
  --capture .local/pce-reference/spread-terrain \
  --code .local/pce-reference/spread-terrain/code-002160.bin
```

## Returning weapon (ID 2)

`bc_return_fire`, `bc_return_step` and `bc_aim16` translate $947D–$964F and
$82BE–$837A. The returning shot travels straight for 16 updates, then chooses
one of sixteen fixed-point velocities toward the player's current coordinates.
The source uses one's-complement magnitudes for negative aiming deltas; the
native classifier preserves that bias and the original integer ratio thresholds.
The catch test happens before movement. It decrements a separate active counter
and retires the shot through the animation terminator. Its animation has eight
four-update entries, including both hardware flip bits.

`tools/qa_bc_return.py` continuously compared all live slot fields and the active
counter with `.local/pce-reference/return-flight-v2`. Result: 61 launches and
catches, 35 blocked attempts, and 2,089 active slot updates. Both launch directions
and all four usable power tiers were exercised, reaching concurrent limits
2/4/6/8. Moving-player input exercised ten of the sixteen homing directions
(0/1/5/6/7/8/9/10/12/15); the other directions are transcribed but not covered by
this trace. The source switches away from the returning weapon at zero power,
so the initial zero-power capture is not used to claim returning-weapon coverage.

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/qa_bc_return.py \
  --capture .local/pce-reference/return-flight-v2
```

## Shared main-weapon engine

`BcWeapons` / `bc_weapons_step` now integrate all three main weapons and charged
beams in one 30-slot pool. Ordinary allocation searches slots 0–27; beams require
slots 20–24 to be empty. Existing projectiles keep their own behavior when the
selected weapon changes. The engine retains charge/ordinary-fire/beam/update
ordering, updates projectiles during player death, and suspends the weapon task
during player entry. Entry/death branches are transcribed but not yet covered by
the initial integrated captures. Option weapon slots/routines are covered below.

`tools/qa_bc_weapons.py` passed the existing charge/beam, rapid-fire, returning and
cave fixtures through this single entry point. A new mixed-weapon trace passed
700 consecutive frames and 4,402 active slot updates, with 251 ordinary launches,
all four projectile families, two beam releases blocked by occupied slots, and a
successful five-segment beam after the slots cleared. Recoil events match the
source after its later $747F decrement. Sound events are transcribed but audio
playback is not tested. The fixture replays eight source enemy contacts; contact
detection and enemy HP/death are not included in this claim.

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/qa_bc_weapons.py \
  --capture .local/pce-reference/weapon-pool \
  --code .local/pce-reference/code-inspect/code-002160.bin
```

The common projectile hit extents are named `half_x`/`half_y` to match the
source's $A066 and $A09A collision-axis usage. The earlier field names suggested
the opposite axes; this naming correction does not change the stored values.
The integrated engine is still independent of the game-mode flow and renderer.
No playable BC mode or whole-game performance certification is claimed.

## Option units and their weapons

`bc_option_step` translates $9CA8–$9D59. The two units deploy to a 28-pixel
vertical offset over fourteen updates and follow an eight-update coordinate
history. The source stores only the history's low coordinate bytes: option X
retains its spawn high byte, while Y uses the player's current high byte. Each
unit has three HP, changes appearance as it is damaged, and plays a four-frame
explosion after its third hit. The native code retains that layout and timing.
`bc_option_collect` transcribes missing-slot priority, lower-HP replenishment,
upper-slot tie breaking and the full/full no-op. Its pickup application and
differential tests are described below.

`bc_weapons_step` now includes the $9650–$9837 option fire path. Each unit owns
up to two active shots. Straight main fire gives expanding option fire; expanding
main fire gives returning option fire; returning main fire gives straight option
fire. Option power changes at 4. Shots share the ordinary pool and preserve their
owner until retirement, including impact-animation lifetime. Options can fire
on a two-button press before the beam's reserved-slot check. That ordering is
implemented, but this release-conflict branch is not covered by the fixtures yet.

Two easily missed source behaviors were confirmed and retained: powered expanding
option shots still use the small expansion sequence, and straight option shots
retain the previous slot's terrain-probe delay. The returning active counter
includes option returning shots. `bc_weapons_record_position` is separate from
the weapon task because the source shifts its trail after the enemy task.

Evidence:

- `option-bodies`: 702 active option-body updates, six injected hits, all HP values
  3/2/1/0, both facings, and both final retirements match. Options were initialized
  from source templates using reference-only RAM pokes; this does not test pickup
  acquisition. The continuous pool comparison also matches 30 option launches.
- `option-weapons-tasks`: 1,101 consecutive weapon tasks and trail updates, 872 main
  launches, 198 option launches across all three families at powers 3/4 and both
  facings, plus 4,088 native projectile collision scans match the reference.
  No enemy-hit notifications are replayed in this comparison. Enemy positions,
  dimensions and HP still come from source enemy-task entries.
- The earlier mixed main-weapon/beam regression still passes 4,402 active slot
  updates and 1,417 native collision scans after adding options.

The rapid-fire capture exposed a limitation of frame-end RAM comparisons: the
original cooperative tasks can cross the video-frame boundary. Some captures
contain enemy scans both before and after a weapon task within one frame number.
`--contact-trace` now also records `weapon-tasks.bin` in actual execution order.
`tools/qa_bc_weapon_tasks.py` continuously carries native pool state across weapon,
collision and trail tasks and compares completed tasks, instead of assuming a
fixed order relative to video snapshots. Each record is frame (u32 LE), task
kind (u8), X (u8), and 8,192 bytes of RAM. Kinds 0/1 are weapon entry/exit, 2 is
trail entry, and 3/4/5 are collision entry/normal exit/depleted exit. Source task
tracing is currently verified on round 1. Initial frame-based option stress
captures are retained for diagnosis, not claimed as passing continuous tests.

This covers option bodies and firing, not full BC integration, multiplayer
targeting, a playable remaster, or whole-game performance.

## Pickup application and option replenishment

`bc_pickup_apply` translates $8990–$8A28 for all nine item IDs. It preserves the
five-step bonus chain (score commands 3/5/7/9/11), weapon selection with byte-sized
power increments, option collection, fixed score commands 16/14/12, and extra-life
and life-pickup counter increments. Power and life counters wrap at 256. Pickup
events expose consumption, score and sound commands, selected option slot and
life-display refresh. Score accumulation and threshold lives are covered separately
below; sound playback and HUD rendering remain unfinished.

`tools/qa_bc_pickups.py` passes 2,191 original-routine cases across all item IDs,
including 1,108 option refills (247 upper / 861 lower), 41 full/full no-ops and
165 counter-wrap cases. It compares inventory mutations, every represented
option-body field, retained fractional coordinates, HP and side, and captures
the actual score/sound command arguments from the original RAM-resident stubs.
The option cases cover missing/dying/living lower slots, all HP combinations
1..3, lower-HP priority, ties and maximum HP. The default missing-both case covers
upper-slot initialization. These tests verify pickup application independently
of collectible spawning and the still-unfinished stage engine.

The fixture uses `--player-trace --pickup-cases`. It replaces contact inputs
temporarily, lets the original pickup handler execute, then restores inventory,
enemy and option fields before normal tasks resume. It is incompatible with
`--player-cases` in the same capture. Source scoring can run its own threshold
awards, so the verifier excludes the life field for score-only items; it verifies
the direct extra-life item's counters separately. This pickup comparison alone does
not certify score accumulation or a complete playthrough; score processing is covered below.

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/qa_bc_pickups.py \
  --capture .local/pce-reference/pickup-cases
```

## Native projectile-to-enemy collision

`bc_enemy_shots` translates $A01E–$A0E6. It scans slots 0–27 in source order,
rejects disabled/offscreen projectiles, applies strict overlap bounds with the
original byte-sized hitbox sums, consumes non-piercing shots even when damage is
blocked, and stops after the first damaging hit. HP subtraction preserves byte
underflow. The returned `depleted` event means the current HP is exhausted; it
is **not** a completed enemy death, especially for bosses with multiple bars.
Movement, cooldown decrement, score, death/phase handlers and player contact are
outside this function.

The oracle's optional `--contact-trace` records RAM at instruction-fetch entry
$A01E, normal exit $A0E9, or HP-exhaustion entry $A1DF. PC checks exclude reads
of those addresses as data, and entry/exit records are buffered into complete
pairs. `contacts.bin` uses a little-endian 32-bit frame, enemy slot byte, phase
byte (0 entry / 1 normal / 2 exhausted), then 8,192 bytes of RAM per record.
The initial boss capture contained a dangling data-read entry and is not used;
`boss-contacts-verified` is the capture with instruction-fetch filtering.

`tools/qa_bc_contacts.py` passed:

| Fixture | Scans | Damaging hits | HP exhausted | Consumed shots | Protected contact scans | Piercing damage hits |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| enemy-contacts | 1,418 | 8 | 3 | 8 | 0 | 0 |
| boss-contacts-verified | 20,732 | 50 | 0 | 0 | 366 | 50 |

The integrated `qa_bc_weapons.py` now uses these native collision scans when a
`contacts.bin` accompanies a full-state capture. `enemy-contacts` passed 700
consecutive frames, 4,402 active projectile updates and 1,417 collision scans
(the first snapshot initializes the test), **with zero replayed hit notifications**.
Enemy coordinates and target fields still come from the original engine's scan
entry snapshots. This verifies native weapon evolution plus collision/damage,
not native enemy movement or whole-stage simulation. Fixtures without collision
snapshots retain the explicitly reported hit-notification replay fallback.

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/qa_bc_contacts.py \
  --capture .local/pce-reference/boss-contacts-verified
.venv/bin/python tools/qa_bc_weapons.py \
  --capture .local/pce-reference/enemy-contacts \
  --code .local/pce-reference/code-inspect/code-002160.bin
```

## Common enemy animation and motion

`bc_enemy_motion` translates $9EB1–$A009: byte-sized animation timers,
animation-loop records, ordinary sprite offsets/flips, composite-frame records,
24-bit fixed-point movement, movement delays, offscreen retirement and the limited
object counter. A dying object advances its animation without movement. These
are animation-data records, not emulated CPU instructions. Sprite-group bases
can live in source work RAM ($3692 was observed), so the native state receives a
resolved base rather than assuming that the group table is immutable ROM.

`bc_enemy_depleted` translates $A1DF–$A217 and emits a score-code event when
entering the death state. The boss-bar refill branch is transcribed but **not yet
exercised** by these captures; do not treat it as verified boss-phase behavior.
Score accumulation is covered below; enemy-specific death routines remain unfinished.

The `--enemy-trace` oracle option captures paired entry/exit work-RAM snapshots
for these routines. `tools/qa_bc_enemies.py` compared every exposed state field:

| Fixture | Common updates | Retirements | Dying updates | Composite updates | Delayed updates | HP exhaustions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| enemy-motion-verified | 1,748 | 9 | 321 | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| enemy-boss-motion | 18,974 | 136 | 231 | 0 | 0 | 5 |
| enemy-composite | 13,755 | 168 | 485 | 3,074 | 397 | 17 |

The latter two fixtures repeatedly set source enemy HP to 1 before updates to
reach transitions sooner. The routines themselves are unchanged; this validates
individual transitions, **not original difficulty, whole bosses or a playthrough**.
The first attempt `enemy-motion` is superseded by `enemy-motion-verified`, which
captures the HP-exhaustion routine after its final damage-lock decrement.

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/qa_bc_enemies.py \
  --capture .local/pce-reference/enemy-composite \
  --code .local/pce-reference/enemy-composite/code-002160.bin
```

Enemy-specific AI still supplies each common routine's incoming state in these
tests. The native code is not yet a complete enemy simulation or playable mode.

## Enemy allocation, templates and shot birth

`src/bc_world.c` / `inc/bc_world.h` now define the source's 32-slot actor pool
and native factory primitives. `bc_actor_allocate` translates the forward and
reverse searches at $8119/$8128, treating any nonzero state as occupied and
returning failure without changing the pool. `bc_actor_template` translates
$8137–$81C5. It initializes the original 19-byte template fields and clears only
the fields the source clears. Positions, velocities, fractional coordinates,
damage lock and family scratch fields survive slot reuse. Ordinary templates
retain the prior bar count; composite templates set bars and current HP to ten.
The represented routine addresses are native-dispatch identifiers, not executable
HuC6280 instructions. Sprite bases are resolved from the stage's RAM/ROM references.

`bc_actor_spawn_bullet` translates $8A29–$8A57: allocate forward, apply the shot
template, copy only the parent's integer position, retain the child's fractional
position, and select velocity from the original speed/direction tables. It returns
before the immediate common update and later limited-shot counter increment;
the future world task must execute those operations in their source order.

`--factory-trace` records allocation/template entry and exit pairs in `factory.bin`
and shot birth pairs in `bullet-birth.bin`. `tools/qa_bc_factory.py` compares native
results and every represented actor field. The factory supports the observed
round-1 and relocated later-round routines. Passing captures:

| Capture | Forward/reverse searches | Full-pool failures | Templates | Composite templates | Shot births / failed births |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `factory-round1` | 159 / 1 | 0 | 160 | 0 | not traced |
| `factory-composite` (round 9) | 253 / 0 | 0 | 255 | 2 | 35 / 0 |
| `factory-boss-spawns` (round 10) | 160 / 0 | 4 | 164 | 0 | 156 / 4 |

The shot-birth comparisons cover all sixteen directions, 154 births with retained
nonzero fractions, and four exhausted-pool returns with no actor changes. The
template comparisons include 454 applications with fractional positions. No
captured template reused a nonzero damage lock, so that preservation is transcribed
but not claimed as exercised. These captures use debug invulnerability and do not
certify a native stage scheduler, enemy runtime, multiplayer pool sizing or speed.

## Integrated common enemy task

`bc_actor_common` connects native animation/motion, cooldown, shot collision,
HP exhaustion, player contact, option absorption, pickup effects and the final
damage-lock tick in the original $9EB1–$A217 order. The player state now groups
coordinates, inventory and the weapon pool. The common task emits score, sound,
life-display and contact events for the future world scheduler.

Important ordering is preserved: retirement returns before damage-lock ticking;
dying actors skip movement/collision but still tick the lock; a non-living player
suppresses cooldown and collision work; cooldown 1 expires before the collision
scan, while 255 is permanent; HP depletion returns before player contact; boss-bar
refill includes exactly one lock tick. Option absorption schedules its weapon-pool
slot's impact handler. A consumed pickup clears the actor but still takes the
source's final lock tick. This is the original single-player common task; the
multiplayer world policy is still to be integrated and verified.

`--common-trace` records entry at $9EB1 and complete exits at $9EDA/$A217 in
`common.bin`, using the paired 8,198-byte record layout. `tools/qa_bc_common.py`
compares all represented actor and projectile fields, player/inventory state,
limited-shot count and score-queue commands:

| Capture | Complete updates | Retirements | Score events | Player deaths | Option absorptions | Boss-bar refills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `common-natural` | 2,676 | 15 | 11 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| `common-cases` | 1,594 | 604 | 330 | 385 | 165 | 55 |

The natural fixture uses ordinary fire without debug invincibility. The controlled
fixture (`--common-trace --common-cases`) temporarily injects inputs before the
complete common task, then restores affected actor, player and projectile fields
after its exit. It exercises all nine pickups (494 consumed), permanent protection,
cooldown expiry, player death, dying actors, both retirement paths, depletion before
contact, option priority, and final/nonfinal boss bars. It is incompatible with
the narrower player/pickup fixtures. No artificial mutation occurs midway through
the common task. The 55 observed boss-bar refills now cover the branch that the
earlier isolated enemy-motion captures did not exercise.

Family AI, stage scheduling, death/checkpoint flow, graphics and multiplayer remain
outside this comparison. A complete common task is not a playable BC mode or a
performance result. Score accumulation and audio/HUD execution remain separate.

## Score queue, decimal arithmetic and extra lives

`src/bc_score.c` translates queue insertion at $3D7E–$3D90 and the score task at
$6CB3–$6D3B. The 16-slot queue retains the original wrap-and-overwrite behavior and
$FF empty sentinel. Queue insertion is disabled when the original playing flag
is zero. Each score iteration advances the RNG, consumes at most one command,
adds seven decimal digits with discarded overflow, and then compares all eight
score bytes with the high score. An empty queue can still update the high score.

Extra lives are awarded at 50,000, 100,000, 200,000, 400,000, 800,000, 1,200,000,
1,600,000, 2,000,000 and 4,000,000; the tenth threshold is the source's unreachable
eight-digit sentinel for valid seven-digit scores. At most one threshold is
awarded per consumed command. Lives retain the source's byte wrapping. Sound and
HUD refreshes are emitted as events; playback and rendering are not implemented
by this module. Threshold state is expected to be a valid source index 0..9.

The original eight-bit command-address calculation aliases nonempty command IDs
modulo 32. IDs 26..31 read the first six adjacent threshold records. The native
table preserves this behavior; those aliases are not new collectible types.

`--score-trace` captures paired complete score iterations and enqueue calls in
`score.bin`. `tools/qa_bc_score.py` passes:

- `score-natural`: 2,674 iterations and 11 enqueue/consume calls from ordinary
  gameplay. This short run does not reach an extra-life threshold.
- `score-cases`: 1,189 controlled iterations, all 255 nonempty command values,
  all ten threshold indices, 1,103 extra-life awards, 739 high-score updates and
  four score-overflow cases. Seven enqueue checks include three ignored calls,
  occupied-slot overwrite and producer-index wrap. Cases also exercise the empty
  sentinel, threshold equality and either side, high-score comparisons, and lives
  wrapping from 255 to zero.

The controlled fixture uses `--score-trace --score-cases`, temporarily replacing
score-task or enqueue inputs and restoring them after the original routine exits.
It is isolated branch evidence, not a high-scoring playthrough. The native module
is ready to consume the common enemy task's score events but is not yet connected
to a complete BC world scheduler or player HUD.

## Player control, death and entry

`src/bc_player.c` translates player control at $8F29–$90B7 and pose/countdown
selection at $740D–$7485. `bc_player_step` runs control, weapons and pose in source
order, returning early for the checkpoint jump. Entry preserves fractional
coordinates and advances two pixels per update. Death clears the weapon states
on the first update, selects explosion frames every eight updates, and requests
checkpoint reconstruction at the original timer value. Pose selection retains
source frame identifiers for the future Genesis renderer. Recoil and protection
countdowns run after weapon processing.

`--player-flow-trace` records control and pose entry/exit pairs. The natural
`player-flow-natural` capture passes 1,680 control updates and 1,677 pose updates,
including 144 entry updates, 123 dying updates, 360 dead waiting updates and three
checkpoint requests. This fixture has no terrain-crush event.

With `--common-trace`, the oracle also writes ordered `player-runtime.bin` events.
`tools/qa_bc_player_runtime.py` carries native player and weapon state through
1,680 player updates, 2,687 common enemy updates and 1,677 option-history updates
in `player-runtime-natural`. It matches 263 main shots and three player deaths
without replaying source hit notifications into the native pool. Source RAM is
used to initialize the three life segments; checkpoint reconstruction is still
unported. Enemy-family AI remains a source input at common-task entry. The trace
does not certify a native stage scheduler, rendering, multiplayer or performance.

Both host comparisons pass and the module compiles with the Genesis toolchain.
It is not yet called by the game runtime, so the ROM build is not performance
or playable-mode evidence.

## Player initialization on stage restart

`bc_player_reset` implements the player portion of $65D6–$6622. It clears the
30-slot weapon pool, charge, owned-shot counters and bonus chain, then decodes
the original 32-byte player template. Held-fire state, the shoot latch, option
history, lives and life-pickup count survive this operation because they are
outside the original clear ranges. Round 10 (internal index 9) preserves the
incoming weapon and power; other rounds select those fields from the template.

The player-flow oracle now records paired initialization snapshots in
`player-reset.bin`. `qa_bc_player_reset.py` matches three natural resets in

## Checkpoint camera and stage event gate

`src/bc_stage.c` translates checkpoint header initialization ($6786), camera and
script restoration ($737C–$73A0), and fractional scroll ($6ED4–$6F0C). Camera
coordinates wrap at 4,096 pixels with eight fractional bits. The original
checkpoint stores the integer high bytes of X/Y and a stage-script pointer;
restoring it zeros both lower coordinate bytes and reloads terrain attributes.

The event gate ($7690–$76D2) compares a script record against the camera's low
integer byte, choosing Y when vertical velocity is nonzero and X otherwise.
Matching records yield a handler identifier. The caller must execute the native
handler, advance the script by three bytes with `bc_stage_event_complete`, then
check again in the same update. `FF FF` stops processing; `FF FE` advances two
bytes and ends processing for that update, only when the position byte matches.
Actual stage handlers are not implemented by this gate.

`--player-flow-trace` also records `stage-state.bin`; the stage hooks verify the
loaded code signature and cover the later-round relocation by -$217.
`qa_bc_stage.py` matches:

- `stage-state-natural`: one initialization, three restores and 1,680 scroll updates.
- `stage-events-natural`: one initialization/restore, 4,008 scroll updates,
  4,094 event checks and 86 handler dispatches in round 1.
- `stage-events-round4-relocated`: one initialization/restore, 4,008 scroll updates,
  4,088 event checks and 80 handler dispatches in round 4.

The earlier `stage-events-round4` capture used incorrect unrelocated hooks and is
invalid evidence. Both event captures use reference invulnerability to extend
observation. All observed velocities are (+85, 0) in 8.8 units; vertical, negative,
wrap and sentinel branches still need source coverage. These checks compare the
camera/event gate in isolation, with source handlers providing their effects;
they do not certify a native stage scheduler or rendering. The Genesis build
compiles the module cleanly but does not yet invoke it during gameplay.

## Ordered native actor loop

`bc_runtime_actor_loop` scans active slots in ascending order, matching
$9E17–$9E27. It reads each slot when reached, so a child born into a later slot
receives its normal update in the same loop after its immediate birth update.
The callback exposes each completed actor result for the future score/audio
scheduler. An unsupported handler returns that slot without processing it or
subsequent slots; earlier completed updates remain applied. Completion returns 32.

AI tracing now records `actor-loop.bin` around the full source loop.
`qa_bc_actor_loop.py` seeds state once per loop, then compares the full actor pool,
player state/inventory, projectile bodies/counters, limited-shot count and RNG
against the source exit. `actor-loop-round1` passes 3,475 complete loops with
22,307 actor updates, 16 child birth updates, four later-slot child updates,
two player deaths and 75 retirements. No unsupported loop occurs in this capture.
This is stronger than per-actor comparison, but stage, player and score tasks
still provide external inputs between loops; it is not a continuous native
playthrough. Score/audio callback execution and the unsupported-loop return path
still need scheduler-level execution coverage. The Genesis build passes, with
no 60 fps performance claim.

`bc_runtime_actor_events` now provides a native loop sink that inserts child
score commands before the parent's command and can forward the completed event
to another consumer. It honors the original playing flag through
`bc_score_enqueue`; score accumulation remains a separate task. Stage-event
execution likewise queues score commands from immediate birth updates when a
score state is supplied.

The enemy-loop and stage-event verifiers now compare the complete score state,
including all 16 queue cells and both indices. The original loop fixture still
passes 3,475 loops, but emits zero score commands; the stage fixture also has no
awards. These checks alone cover preservation, not score delivery. The first
firing fixture, `actor-loop-scoring`, is invalid as a whole-loop comparison:
its scripted protection write can occur midway through a source loop (observed
at frame 5141), changing player state outside native simulation. A replacement
fixture removes RAM pokes during the measured interval.
`actor-loop-scoring-natural` passes 1,073 complete loops, 3,646 actor updates,
seven score commands, two player deaths and nine retirements. Every score cell
and queue index matches at loop exit. This confirms real command insertion;

forwarded audio/HUD callback. The Genesis build is clean. Score-task scheduling,
playable integration and performance verification remain unfinished.

## Random-number update

`bc_random_next` translates $6D41–$6D65. It multiplies the 16-bit seed by three
modulo 65,536, then adds the old low byte to the resulting high byte, discarding
the carry. `--random-trace` records each original routine's frame, input and
output as an eight-byte little-endian record (`u32, u16, u16`).
`tools/qa_bc_random.py` matches 5,005 calls with 5,005 distinct inputs from
`random-sequence`. This verifies the transition, not complete-game call order:
enemy AI also advances the generator, and most families remain unported.

## Reproduction

Use the extracted, case-corrected CUE and the user's BIOS:

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/pce_oracle.py my-reference \
  --cue .local/pce-reference/disc/reference.cue \
  --bios /Users/rester159/Downloads/syscard3.pce \
  --frames 12000 --stage 0 --invulnerable --boss-fast

.venv/bin/python tools/qa_bc_rules.py \
  --capture .local/pce-reference/charge-rules \
  --code .local/pce-reference/code-inspect/code-002160.bin \
  --motion-capture .local/pce-reference/motion-rules
```

Capture names are never overwritten. `--input` accepts a timeline of
`frame P1 Button I 1`, `frame P1 Right 0`, or
`frame poke 1f00a9 01`; `--trace-from` records per-frame logic snapshots.
Full local source hashes and comparison results are in
`.local/pce-reference/reference-manifest.json`.

## Equivalence boundary

Port the original update order, numerical precision, state transitions, RNG,
enemy/script timing, hitboxes and collision maps. Validate each against original
execution before replacing its renderer. New palettes, tiles, sprite artwork
and HUD placement must not alter those simulation inputs. Keep the original
256-pixel gameplay width when laying it out on the Genesis display.

The existing Home multiplayer extension is not evidence of BC equivalence.
First establish the CD's single-player behavior; any multiplayer extension
must be identified separately. The existing organic-map preview and arcade
game remain separate from this unfinished port.

## Active completion requirements (2026-10-03)

The requested end state remains all three Home modes (Normal, Before Christ,
Boss Rush), each opening a 1/2/3/4-player modal, with remastered BC graphics,
faithful original BC single-player behavior, scaled multiplayer waves and boss
energy, and verified 60 fps / 100% speed on an unoverclocked Genesis.

Normal and Boss Rush now open the player modal; cancelling preserves the saved
count, confirming persists it, and all selected players start together. One-player
sessions exclude other slots. Normal now starts the actual arcade stage timeline;
the unfinished organic background preview no longer replaces ordinary gameplay.
The preview source remains available for development. Before Christ is not yet
exposed as a selectable game because its runtime is incomplete.

The remaining requirements above are not certified by the menu regressions or
isolated BC rule comparisons. In particular, no BC renderer, complete stage engine,
or whole-game performance result has been delivered yet.

Beam trace reproduction (the input timeline holds I and II for 40/50/60 updates,
with 180 idle updates between charges):

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/pce_oracle.py beam-reference \
  --cue .local/pce-reference/disc/reference.cue \
  --bios /Users/rester159/Downloads/syscard3.pce \
  --frames 3900 --input .local/pce-reference/beam-input.txt \
  --trace-from 2100 --full-state --invulnerable
.venv/bin/python tools/qa_bc_beam.py --capture .local/pce-reference/beam-reference
```

`state.bin` is a sequence of little-endian 32-bit frame numbers followed by
8,192 bytes of work RAM. It is an optional companion to the existing compact
`logic.bin` format, which is unchanged.

## Combined gameplay task comparison

`bc_runtime_play` now runs player control, weapons, pose, the ascending enemy
loop, score insertion and option position history in source order. Checkpoint
requests exit before the enemy loop; unsupported actors return an explicit
incomplete status. Stage dispatch, camera scrolling, score consumption and
checkpoint reconstruction remain separate and are not covered by this wrapper.

`qa_bc_play.py` compared 1,075 paired gameplay tasks from `play-task-round1`,
including 164 main shots and two checkpoint exits. Player and weapon state was
carried continuously across each of three life segments. Actor pools, stage
state, RNG and score state were source inputs at each task entry; their resulting
state was compared at exit, along with player state and projectiles. The fixture
uses no artificial RAM writes during the measured interval. All tested tasks
matched, with no unsupported actors. This is a bounded round-one comparison,
not proof of whole-game equivalence or Genesis frame rate.

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/qa_bc_play.py \
  --capture .local/pce-reference/play-task-round1 \
  --code .local/pce-reference/play-task-round1/code-002160.bin
```

The $AA8E/$AB88 attacker now uses the shared steering implementation with its
own $ABC9/$ABDC animations and original routine addresses. Its five spawn events
($AA34/$AA3A/$AA40/$AA46/$AA4C) use template $ABB1 and an initial horizontal
velocity of -640 (8.8), preserving reused coordinate fractions and source field
initialization. Stage resources provide its sprite base separately. The $AA23
checkpoint event now writes checkpoint (9,0) and script $A5DC before advancing
past the event.

The existing `actor-step-hopper` source comparison now passes 115,417 supported
actor updates, including 1,801 updates at $AA8E and 1,036 at $AB88. The former
covers phases 0/1/2/3 with 510/680/130/481 updates. The remaining 7,216 unsupported
updates in that fixture are boss handlers $B3BF/$B471/$B3E3/$B488; they remain
explicitly unsupported rather than approximated.

The new `stage-runtime-fast-curve` capture passes 106 stage events, including
17 faster-attacker births across all five lanes and one $AA23 checkpoint change.
It compares the complete actor pool and stage/player/score state per event.
Four event handlers remain unsupported in that capture ($8D76, $8D22, $414C,
$B34B). No allocation failure or scoring command occurred in this fixture.
The 1,075-task continuous-player gameplay regression still passes. The SGDK
release build completes without compiler warnings. These comparisons do not
establish a complete playable BC stage or hardware performance.

## First boss entry and living updates

Round-one event $B34B now creates both boss parts in slots 0/1, preserves their
coordinate fractions, initializes their damage locks, sets boss-active to $FF,
and executes both immediate common updates. `BcStage` retains the boss-active
byte. Stage resources now include the boss sprite base, and the event result
retains each part's common event for score/audio consumers.

The living $B3BF/$B3E3 and $B471/$B488 routines now implement the startup damage
lock, vertical tracking/dead zone, separate attack countdowns, eight-projectile
spreads, two homing missiles, allocation-failure exits, and the second part's
position/lock synchronization. Boss shots execute common updates immediately
without incrementing the ordinary limited-shot counter. The actor result
retains up to ten extra child events in source order; the runtime score sink
inserts their commands before the parent command. The $B5C2 projectile revival
handler is translated but was not exercised by the available fixture.

`actor-step-hopper` now passes all 122,633 actor updates with zero unsupported
handlers. This includes 128 startup and 3,480 active updates for each boss part.
The comparison seeds source state per actor task and compares the full actor
pool, including newly spawned children, plus player/projectile/RNG/count state.
It is not a continuous native boss-fight or performance test. The boss-inactive
speed/cadence branch and projectile revival remain unverified by this fixture.

`stage-runtime-fast-curve` now passes 107 events, including the two-part boss
entry; only $8D76/$8D22/$414C remain unsupported in that capture. The reported
105 birth events count the boss entry once, although it initializes two parts.
The continuous-player 1,075-task regression still passes, and the SGDK release
build completes without warnings. Boss defeat ($B497 and its scheduled effects),
round completion, renderer integration, and the requested hardware frame-rate
verification remain outstanding. The larger multi-child event results also
need profiling when this runtime is wired into the Genesis frame loop.

## Boss loop ordering and defeat handoff

`boss-loop-natural` compares 398 complete enemy loops with 2,597 actor updates,
28 immediate child updates, and 28 later-slot updates of those same children.
It includes one player death and 27 retirements. All actor/player/projectile,
RNG, limited-shot and score state comparisons passed. The input fixture stops
protection-timer writes before the measured interval. The loop and combined-play
verifiers now supply boss state and both boss projectile sprite bases explicitly.

The $B497 defeat handler clears non-pickup actors in slots 2–31, marks the second
boss part dying, records the effect-center Y, requests the source task-2 defeat
sequence and sound 13, and initializes the main part's 80-update disappearance.
The secondary part's $8E78 disappearance handler is also translated. These are
native actor updates and an explicit scheduler handoff: the scheduled 50 groups
of three unpaused waits, explosion births, and subsequent stage transition are
not yet implemented by the runtime.

`boss-defeat-task` injects state $40 into the first boss part at frame 7600 to
exercise the defeat path. It passes 1,925 actor tasks, including one $B497 and
one $8E78 invocation, 52 retirements, and the expected effect center/sound. It
has no unsupported actor handlers. This controlled fixture verifies defeat
cleanup, not natural weapon damage reaching defeat or the still-unported
scheduled effects. Source-scheduled explosions remain inputs at task boundaries.

Ordinary actor updates no longer clear all ten unused child-event records.
Only entries below `extra_count` are initialized and valid. Whole-loop and
combined-play regressions cover this change, but its hardware cost and the
remaining result-copy overhead still require profiling in a playable BC loop.

## Boss-defeat explosion factory and cadence

`bc_actor_spawn_boss_effect` translates $8DE3-$8E59. It allocates before
advancing RNG, uses template $8F02, consumes two random values for the source's
X/Y distribution, preserves slot coordinate fractions, and zeros velocity.
The caller executes the immediate common update after successful allocation.

`bc_runtime_defeat_begin/tick` represents the first phase of task 2: fifty
allocation attempts separated by three unpaused scheduler ticks. The final
attempt returns a distinct completion result; it does not silently implement
the subsequent music/CD or stage transition. These functions still need to be
connected to the playable Genesis task scheduler and defeat event sink.

`boss-effects-birth` captures the controlled defeat at frame 7600, followed by
50 births at frames 7603 through 7750. `qa_bc_boss_effects.py` verifies the
complete pool and RNG at each birth and compares native countdown emissions
against those observed frames. All 50 births matched, all 50 positions were
distinct, and all reused nonzero coordinate fractions. No allocation failures,
pause intervals, or later-round relocation occurred in this fixture. Thus the
unpaused cadence and birth data are verified; those other branches and full
scheduler integration remain unverified. SGDK compilation passes without
warnings after these additions.

## Native defeat-event/task integration

`BcRuntimeEvents` can now own a defeat sequence. The actor event sink starts
that sequence from a real boss-defeat event, preserving the effect-center Y.
`bc_runtime_defeat_step` combines countdown, allocation, immediate common actor
update, and score insertion. On the final attempt it resumes a stopped stage
or reports that the stage transition owner must continue. That transition,
audio/CD work, and wiring into the playable Genesis scheduler remain unfinished.

`boss-effects-task` captures each explosion attempt through its immediate common
update. The combined native task matched all 50 attempts, including the complete
actor pool, player/projectiles, RNG, limited-shot count and score state. Sequence
state carries across attempts; the other task inputs are seeded from the source.
The source hook ends before the final resume/transition branch, so that branch
is implemented from disassembly but is not certified by this comparison.

The combined-play verifier additionally passes the same controlled boss-defeat
fixture and confirms that the event sink starts a 50-effect sequence with wait=3
and the source effect center. Player/weapons state carries across those gameplay
tasks; effects between gameplay tasks remain source inputs. This does not yet
prove a continuous native fight-to-next-stage run. The existing round-one
combined-play regression and SGDK build also pass.

## Cleanup event and result-buffer experiment

Stage handler $8D76 now clears the state of all non-pickup actors, preserving
item actors and the limited-shot counter exactly as the source does. The longer
round-one stage-event fixture now passes 108 events, including this cleanup.
$8D22 and $414C remain unsupported in that fixture.

A 68000 code-generation check rejected an attempted explicit output-buffer API
for actor updates. With the release optimization flags, the existing aggregate
return already writes into caller storage. The alternate pointer API generated
six static memcpy call sites versus two in the existing function, and its local
stack frame increased from 92 to 116 bytes. These are assembly observations, not
a timing benchmark. The alternate API was removed and the original retained;
whole boss-loop regressions still pass. Inspection artifacts are
`.local/pce-reference/bc-world-before-buffer.s` and
`.local/pce-reference/bc-world-after-buffer.s`. No frame-rate improvement is
claimed from this experiment; actual Genesis profiling remains required.

## Boss palette stage event

Handler $414C copies 256 bytes from $4FFD into the lower eight color entries of
each of sixteen source palettes, and sets palette-effect flag $5F to one.
`BcPalette` now preserves all 256 source-format palette words and that flag;
`bc_palette_boss` performs the exact partial replacement. Stage event execution
requires an explicit palette destination for this event, retaining unsupported
status when it is absent. Genesis color allocation/rendering is a separate,
still-unfinished consumer of this data.

The longer round-one stage-event verifier now compares the entire palette and
flag on every event, including non-palette events. All 109 supported events
pass; only the $8D22 audio event remains unsupported in this fixture. Palette
cycling/fading, later-stage event variants and graphics remastering are not
implemented by this change. Combined boss-play and defeat-task regressions and
the SGDK build pass after linking the palette module.

## User-directed Genesis artwork (current requirement)

Before Christ must use this port's own Genesis sprite artwork and remastered
background artwork. PC Engine graphics dumps are visual/layout references, not
the final assets to display. Preserve original terrain geometry, routes,
spawn positions, hitboxes and timing independently of the replacement art.
Reuse the existing Genesis robots, including the P3/P4 recolors, and the
corresponding existing Genesis enemy/boss art where available. Missing families
need matching new artwork rather than a silent gameplay substitution.

Aim for richer color separation, shading and highlights within the actual
renderer allocation. The existing renderer uses PAL0/PAL1 for backgrounds and
PAL2/PAL3 for actors, and its VIVID mode already provides a saturation/brightness
mapping. That is the starting budget, not evidence of extra hardware palette
capacity. Preserve clear silhouettes and player-color identification in 4P;
background detail must not make bullets harder to read. Author new palettes
with VIVID mapping in mind to avoid clipping several shades into one color.
Any raster palette expansion requires measured DMA/scanline cost and must not
compromise the requested 60 fps or simulation speed. No such expansion is yet
implemented or promised.

The initial rendering milestone should therefore pair the original stage's
geometry and native simulation with Genesis assets. A converted PCE screenshot
or tile dump is not a completed visual port or a substitute for this remaster.

## Genesis robot-art adapter

`bc_robot_art_init` maps the source's idle, recoil, two entry poses and five
death-frame selections onto the existing Genesis robot and explosion assets.
`bc_robot_draw` submits those assets through the normal `spr_32` cache. P1/P3
share the first robot; P2/P4 share the second, using the existing 0/4/3/7 color
variants. This is a visual adapter, not four-player BC simulation. Enemy and
background renderers and a playable BC scene are still missing.

BC coordinates describe sprite centers; the adapter converts to Genesis
32x32 top-left coordinates with a caller-selected viewport origin. It handles
signed offscreen entry coordinates and suppresses reset states with no selected
body frame. Unknown nonzero frames remain explicit failures. Five selected
Genesis explosion frames span the BC death sequence without changing its
source-selected frame durations.

`qa_bc_robot_art.py` checks 3,332 visible and 964 hidden/reset player states,
covering all nine source frames and all four player variants. Simulation bytes
are unchanged by every selection. This verifies mapping coverage and coordinate
conversion, not rendered visual quality or SAT upload timing. The SGDK build
passes with the adapter linked.

## Boss countdown in combined gameplay

Inspection of $9E0B-$9E15 found that the source decrements boss-active every
four scheduler-counter ticks before entering the enemy loop. The earlier
per-actor/loop comparisons seeded the already-updated counter and therefore
did not cover this operation. `bc_runtime_play` now performs it and gives the
resulting value to boss AI. Combined-play QA compares the resulting stage byte
as well as actors, and both the 205-task boss fixture and 1,075-task round-one
fixture pass. The clock is an explicit source scheduler-counter input; its
future Genesis scheduling must preserve that phase.

## Audio event handoff

The stage runtime recognizes the fourteen shared playback handlers from $8C50
through $8D61. It retains their exact eight-byte BIOS parameter blocks in a
`BcAudioRequest` and returns a waiting status without advancing the script.
Only backend acknowledgement allows the script to advance. No Genesis music
backend is yet attached, so this does not provide audible BC playback.
Stage-event QA checks source BIOS parameters and unchanged simulation while
waiting, then supplies a test acknowledgement. All events in the longer
round-one fixture are now accounted for under that test contract. Actual audio,
backend latency and continuous game scheduling remain unverified.

An emulator-controlled debug view now submits BC-selected robot poses through

## Stage-owned Genesis background maps

`bg_set_stage` selects an explicit artwork set without Normal mode's camera-zone
selection or Home parallax bands. It reuses the current metatile cache, strip
streaming, plane shadow and DMA pipeline. An optional 16,384-byte BC cell map
is read in its original 256-pixel block order, with coordinates wrapping at
4096 pixels. A 256-entry remap selects Genesis metatiles and flips independently
of source collision attributes. Invalid artwork entries draw blank rather than
reading beyond the supplied tiles. Both full-screen loading and incremental
scrolling use this mapping. Normal zone selection and video reset exit this mode.

`tools/qa_bc_background.py` tests the actual built ROM with a synthetic block map
and existing Genesis tiles. Ten camera positions exercise subcell scroll,
32/256-pixel boundaries, positive and negative world wrapping, and teleports.
It checks 12,640 nametable entries against independently calculated addresses,
metatile templates and flips, including the uploaded VRAM words. Return to the
menu passes. The robot/projectile rendering regression also passes. These are
renderer integration checks, not finished remastered scenery, source-map visual
fidelity, a playable BC stage, or proof of 60 fps with four players. The real
round maps still need their authored Genesis artwork/remaps and runtime wiring.
The existing 4P regression passes after this renderer change: joining, scaled
wave count, Boss Rush health, save/reload, older-save migration and merging.

## Joined native stage and gameplay task

`bc_runtime_frame` now executes due stage events, camera scroll, and the native
player/weapon/enemy task in source order. It binds collision to the updated
camera and the stage's current terrain attribute table. A stop event still
allows this iteration's scroll, matching the entry gate at $6ECA; later tasks
skip scrolling. A retained `BcFrameCursor` preserves that distinction when an
audio request suspends the stage script. Waiting does not run player/enemy
updates, and retrying an unacknowledged request does not mutate gameplay state.
Unknown handlers and a 256-event script guard return explicit failure statuses.
The cursor must be zeroed on a new stage/checkpoint, not on an audio retry.

`qa_bc_play.py --full-frame` passes 1,075 tasks, including 26 stage events,
164 main shots, two checkpoint requests and two test audio acknowledgements.
Player, weapon, enemy and stage state carry between tasks in each of three
source-initialized life segments. The source can execute two updates within
one captured video frame after loading a checkpoint, so task association uses
ordered scroll boundaries rather than one record per frame number. A separate
stop-then-audio contract check verifies one final scroll after acknowledgement
and no scroll on the following task. Earlier play-only round-one and boss-defeat
fixtures still pass.

This is not a complete native scheduler: score/RNG and scheduler-counter inputs
still come from source task boundaries, checkpoint loading initializes the next
segment, and independent palette animation is excluded. No actual Genesis audio
backend, menu-connected BC scene, later-round coverage or 4P timing result is
implied. The next integration work must retain these outstanding requirements.

## Native round-one development scene in the Genesis ROM

`make bc-data` packages the local round-one oracle lookup data and captured
sprite-base references into ignored `src/gen/bc_data.c`. The generator checks
the round/header/signature and records input hashes in
`.local/pce-reference/native-data.json`. These are lookup tables for translated
native logic; no PCE instructions execute on the Genesis. The data can be
regenerated from `play-task-round1` after cleaning generated assets. Builds
without that optional data retain Normal/Boss Rush; the debug scene reports
missing resources rather than dereferencing absent weak symbols.

`src/bc_scene.c` initializes the source round-one checkpoint, player, actor pool,
score queue and native resources, then runs them through the actual Genesis
main loop. It accepts mapped pad input and renders our robot and weapon assets.
The `dbg_bc_native` hook enters this development scene; leaving it restores the
mode-selection screen. Checkpoint requests, unsupported handlers, malformed
scripts and round transitions remain explicit stop statuses. Audio waits require
an explicit acknowledgement. The scene is absent from the menu because enemy
and background artwork, real audio, stage transitions and multiplayer are not
yet integrated. Its seeded RNG and once-per-update independent tasks do not
claim full source-scheduler equivalence.

`tools/qa_bc_native_scene.py` runs the built ROM on Genesis Plus GX, with explicit
test protection and audio acknowledgements. A warm-up excludes scene loading;
input is driven by native update number for repeatable performance comparisons.
The current 7,000-update run executes 144 stage events, reaches 29 live actors,
has no unsupported-handler/art-mapping stop and returns to the menu. A preceding
9,000-emulated-frame run reached all 32 actor slots. Neither run draws enemies
or scenery, so it cannot certify final rendering capacity or 4P speed.

An early common-task dispatch for handler $9EB1 avoids unrelated family checks
for ordinary projectiles/effects. The fixed 7,000-update comparison improves
from 7,855 emulated frames / 854 missed frames / 534 worst measured lines to
7,773 frames / 772 missed / 498 worst lines. This is about 90% full simulation
speed in this limited 1P test, **not** the requested 60 fps result. The 1,075-task
joined source comparison and boss-defeat actor-step regression pass after the
optimization. Existing 4P regression also passes with the larger native build.

## Cached projectile candidates during enemy updates

Profiling splits the development scene into score/defeat, main simulation, and
drawing using SGDK subticks. Raw V-counter timestamps were rejected because
NTSC counter rollback produced negative intervals. Slow-frame samples identify
simulation as the dominant cost, with robot/weapon drawing a small fraction.

The enemy loop now builds an ordered `BcShotIndex` once from eligible main-shot
slots and caches their integer coordinates. Each enemy scans this smaller list;
shots consumed by earlier enemies are still rejected by their changed state.
Piercing, invulnerable-target consumption and first-damaging-hit order remain
unchanged. Stage births outside the enemy loop use the ordinary scan. A temporary
pointer in `BcWorldPlayer` is restored on both normal and unsupported-handler
returns. Event consumers must not create/move shots or change collision flags
inside that scope; current score/audio event consumers do not do so.

The 1,075-task joined comparison and 398-loop natural boss fixture pass with
the cache, including 28 children updated later in their birth iteration.
`qa_bc_shot_index.py` additionally compares cached and ordinary sequential scans
over 32,000 cases: 5,336 contacts and 2,070 damaging hits, checking every weapon
byte after each enemy. Cases include locks, piercing, ordinary-shot consumption,
offscreen coordinates and half-size overflow. Temporary-pointer restoration is
checked for supported and unsupported loops. Robot/projectile rendering and
existing 4P multiplayer regressions also pass.

With the same profiling instrumentation, 7,000 native updates improve from
7,844 emulated frames / 843 misses to 7,317 / 316 misses (144 stage events and
29 peak actors in both). The slot-only variant had 315 misses but a worse
maximum measured frame; coordinate caching retains the lower measured peak.
The resulting roughly 95.7% simulation speed is still below 100%, before adding
enemy/background drawing or multiplayer. No full-game performance requirement
is claimed satisfied by these measurements.

## Frame-context copies and conservative collision bounds

The frame path now updates its mutable `BcActorStepData` in place, avoiding two
whole-context copies per update. Camera, terrain-table pointer and boss-active
countdown are frame-local values; callers must retain a separate context for
each running session. The joined verifier checks these updated values against
the resulting stage state. Round-one and boss-defeat play comparisons pass.
With the same profiling enabled, the 7,000-update scene improves from 316 missed
frames to 203 after this change.

`BcShotIndex` also holds conservative bounds over eligible shot centers and
their largest half-sizes. Enemies outside this area return before individual
tests. Bounds use unwrapped half-size sums; the exact original byte-wrap rule
is still applied to each potential hit. Consumed shots may leave the bounds
larger than necessary, which cannot introduce a missed hit. The 32,000-case
differential check, joined stage/player/enemy fixture and natural boss-loop
fixture still pass. The measured instrumented run drops to 197 missed frames.

Detailed phase timing is now optional (`qa_bc_native_scene.py --profile`), with
`dbg_bc_native_profile_on` off by default. Without this instrumentation, the
current build completes 7,000 updates in 7,181 emulated frames, with 180 missed
frames, 144 stage events and 29 peak actors. This is roughly 97.5% speed in the
incomplete 1P development scene, not 100% speed or a final rendering benchmark.
Existing 4P menu/gameplay/save regression passes after these changes. Remaining
spikes and the missing content/multiplayer integration still require work.

## Actor artwork selection cache

`bc_actors_draw` retains each slot's resolved artwork until its source frame,
sprite base, base reference, attributes or composite-boss flag changes. It
refreshes coordinates from current simulation state on every draw. Inactive
slots submit nothing; all inputs affecting art selection are keyed, so slot
reuse and scene re-entry require no cache reset. The cache uses 704 bytes on
the Genesis build and does not change the simulation or sprite bank.

`qa_bc_actor_cache.py` compares the actual draw implementation with fresh art
resolution over 1,200 updates / 4,004 submissions, varying keys independently,
coordinates, viewport offsets and slot activity. Submission order, fields,
unmapped counts and unchanged simulation bytes pass. Native art inspection

defeat/audio state is cancelled on restart. The debug death input exists only
for exercising this path. The actual continue screen and loading presentation
remain unfinished; status 7 is currently a stopped development scene.

reinstalls the regular HUD through `hud_init`.

## Actor sound event consumption

The native scene now buffers actor sounds during `bc_runtime_frame` and submits
them after the returned player effects. Within each actor event, setup sound
precedes immediate extra children, the single child, and the parent's common
result. Only `extra_count` child entries are read. The 128-byte source-event
queue preserves order and reports overflow; it never changes simulation data
or waits for the sound driver. Defeat-task common sounds, when present, are
submitted before the main player/enemy frame.

Replacement commands are source 3 to $0F (contact death), 4 to $11 (explosion
or boss damage), 8 to $1C (pickup), 12 to $12 (option absorption), 13 to $14
(boss defeat), and 22 to $1D (extra life). Unknown/rejected commands are counted.
This consumes the ordinary actor-loop events; stage-birth-only sound events,
source sample fidelity and all later-stage audio remain unverified.

`qa_bc_actor_audio.py` checks all 256 mapping inputs, event order, zero-event
suppression, exclusion of unused child records, bounded overflow and unchanged
events. Player-audio and existing 4P regressions pass. The current native run
accepts 73 actor commands, all source 4, with zero drops. Pickup, option, death
and defeat mappings are covered by the queue/mapping test but have not yet all
been exercised as audible native gameplay events.

stride between the two rows of a quadrant. The block map remains code offset

bytes as cell definitions would decode stage scripts as garbage graphics.

## Boss burst allocation scan

The eight-projectile radial burst now resumes its first-free search at the
previous child slot. Each immediate common update can retire that child but
cannot free an earlier actor, so rescanning earlier occupied slots is redundant.
The cursor deliberately stays on the last child rather than advancing past it:
if that child retires immediately, the following birth reuses the same slot,
just as the original search from zero does. Homing births and other allocation
paths remain unchanged.

`qa_bc_burst_allocation.py --reference <prior-world.c>` compares the complete
actor pool, player, counter, seed, and valid event fields to the saved prior
implementation. The local reference is
`.local/pce-reference/bc-world-before-burst-scan.c`, SHA-256
`7d8b707919728b56f71067690ee446fd8c5572138fc71118844a0f196340e559`.
All 6,000 deterministic cases pass, including 41,576 child events, 3,213 cases
with immediate slot reuse, and 857 exhausted-pool cases. The original captured
boss-loop fixture also passes all 398 loops / 2,597 actor updates / 28 child
updates, preserving subsequent source-order execution.

for 7,000 updates: 77 misses (previously 81) and a 381-scanline maximum
(previously 385), with unchanged 144 stage events / 29 peak actors and no
sprite drops or unmapped artwork. Cache/menu-return checks pass. This is still
below sustained 100% speed and does not establish multiplayer performance.

## First boss clear-track delay and loader handoff

New `round-exit.csv` taps in the PCE capture record the clear-track request,
return, delay boundaries, and next-round loader dispatch. The fixture
`.local/pce-reference/round-exit-natural/` uses the existing explicitly forced
boss death at frame 7600; "natural" describes the following source execution,
not a naturally defeated boss. The clear request occurs at 7750, its BIOS return
at 7752, the seven-second delay ends at 8172, and the final one-frame wait
hands off to $6042 at 8173. Round selection increments only later, at 8194.

This corrects a potential translation mistake: $3AB6 is a loop around $3AA8's
60-frame wait, not the ordinary one-frame wait. A parameter of seven therefore
means 420 frames, followed by $3A88's one frame and the pause check. During the
wait, $50 inhibits new pause requests ($76E5), rather than freezing all gameplay.
A second source capture with an isolated $4F poke did not create a paused exit:
$7738 cleared it. It is not evidence for the paused branch.

`bc_round_exit` implements the verified audio acknowledgement, pause-inhibit
state, 421-frame delay, pause gate, and one-shot loader handoff. Its unit test
matches the captured boundaries and separately exercises the decoded pause
branch. The native scene now continues its ordinary world updates during this
clear sequence rather than stopping immediately after the explosion sequence.
Our existing finite Genesis jingle $2A is the replacement for the exact
`08 09 40 40 08 15 33 43` PCE request; it is an intentional soundtrack mapping,
not a claim of equivalent recordings or timing. Audio enqueue acknowledgement
continues to be required before the clear delay starts.

`qa_bc_round_exit_scene.py` explicitly forces a boss defeat after 5,500 native
updates, observes phases 0/1/2/3, checks exactly 421 native frame-counter steps
between audio acknowledgement and loader handoff, verifies the third music
command is $2A, and returns to the menu. It passes. This does not load round
two: development status 6 now means the clear sequence has finished and the
next-round loader remains outstanding. Complete pause, fade/loading presentation,
and later-round simulation/art are still required.

structure. This introduced a second call context for the general actor updater,
which had previously been specialized for native per-frame gameplay. Extracting
only the spawn temporaries reduced the benchmark from 212 to 197 misses, but
left most of the regression intact.

were removed to improve speed.

### Terrain and actor dispatch optimization (2026-10-03)

The round-two profile places the largest spikes in crowded pre-boss sections
(ticks roughly 3600–5000), with simulation exceeding drawing time. The terrain
lookup now selects the block/cell bits directly instead of masking each world
coordinate and shifting its high byte twice. The generated 68000 code previously
included an eight-bit shift followed by a variable ten-bit shift per Y probe.
`qa_bc_terrain.py` compares 33,554,432 lookups against the previous source-layout
formula, covering every 16-bit coordinate on either axis against every subcell
row/column, with varied cell/attribute data; all pass.

The general actor dispatcher now classifies a handler once into a single action
instead of keeping sixteen family booleans live. Existing early common/bullet
and round-two specialized paths remain in place. This is an implementation
change only, preserving unsupported-handler rejection and update order.

Unprofiled music-enabled emulator results: round two completes 9,000 updates
in 10,759 frames, with 1,758 missed frames and 426 worst scanlines (previously
1,772 / 429). Round one completes 7,000 updates in 7,081 frames, with 81 misses
and 385 worst scanlines (previously 95 / 388). Both retain zero missing artwork,
sprite drops and runtime remaps and pass menu cleanup. Neither meets sustained
60 fps. A trial reserving the compact HUD's unused weapon-bar tiles for a larger
sprite cache did not improve round-two timing and was removed.

Complete actor-loop captured regressions pass for round-two late creatures
(2,401 loops / 29,805 actor updates), round-two boss combat (4,999 / 108,372),
and round-one boss combat (398 / 2,597). Build/finalization and diff checks pass
without warnings. Logs are `.local/pce-reference/action-opt-*.log` and
`terrain-opt-*.log`. Scenery/progression, multiplayer, frontend integration
and full-speed execution remain unfinished.

The broader round-one `actor-step-hopper` regression also passes all 122,633

the contact function when shots or player contact can be tested. Depleted-enemy
handling retains its own final damage-lock tick and returns immediately.

385 player deaths, 165 option absorptions, 55 boss-bar refills) and 2,676 natural

## Co-op common contact task (not yet scene-integrated)

`bc_actor_party_common_into` adds a 1–4 player common task alongside the existing
single-player entry point. It advances enemy animation/motion once, decrements
cooldown once when a living player exists, visits player slots in order and
emits separate per-player contact/score/audio events. A lethal hit, exhausted
boss bar, consumed pickup or contact-killed ordinary enemy ends that actor's
contact scan; later players cannot hit or claim a removed target. Damage-lock
countdown remains once per actor update, including the depletion helper's own
final tick. Null/dead players do not participate. AI targeting, player lifecycle,
spawn/health scaling and scene integration remain separate required work.

`qa_bc_party_contacts.py` verifies 1/2/3/4-player simultaneous damage without
multiplying enemy speed, lethal-shot ownership, later-shot preservation,
cooldown/permanent-protection/damage-lock clocks, boss-bar exhaustion, inactive
players, exclusive extra-life pickup ownership, independent option absorption,
persistent-boss contact with four players, retirement counters and death clocks.
`qa_bc_common.py --party` compares the new task with source execution at one
player: all 1,594 controlled and 2,676 natural updates pass, including deaths,
options, all pickups, boss bars and score events. The Genesis build and
whitespace checks pass; logs are `.local/pce-reference/party-common-*.log`.

This is the collision foundation, not a playable multiplayer implementation.
The public Home menu still offers Normal and Boss Rush with the shared 1–4
player modal. Before Christ needs its multiplayer update/event integration,
player lifecycle, scaling and performance verification before that menu entry
can truthfully launch the selected player count. No menu behavior changed here.

## Co-op routing through family AI and child updates

`BcWorldPlayer` now has an optional `BcParty` pointer. A shared party contains
up to four player pointers plus an owner-aware contact-event sink. The ordinary
`bc_actor_common_into` entry point dispatches to party contacts only for an
attached 2–4 player party, so existing family AI and immediate child common
updates use the same co-op rules without advancing actors multiple times.
Single-player callers keep a null party pointer and the original behavior.
Party contact events go through the owner-aware sink; they are not duplicated
through the old single-player score/audio event. Shared setup/boss events still
use the existing actor-event path. Context/member pointers must remain stable
through an update, and each party member must be a distinct player object.

The actor loop builds a shot index for every party member and restores all prior
index pointers after completion or an unsupported-handler exit. The four-index
storage lives in a separate co-op function, outside the single-player stack
frame. The ctypes world-player layout was updated with the new pointer.

`qa_bc_party_routing.py` verifies P3 lethal-hit ownership through the production
actor loop, no duplicate score/audio through its legacy sink, restoration of all
four indices on normal/early exits, and P2 contact during the immediate birth
update of the real final boss's eight-bullet burst. The co-op contact cases also
pass. The null-party original common-task cases and final-round captured actor
loop still pass (1,594 controlled common updates; 5,008 loops / 128,454 actor
updates respectively).

The actual Genesis single-player regression completes 4,000 final-round updates
in 6,664 emulator frames, worst work 443 scanlines, with zero missing art, drops
or remaps. This plumbing adds overhead relative to the previous 6,562-frame
build; it is not a performance improvement. Build and whitespace checks pass.
