## Shared co-op player/frame task

`bc_party_bind` binds distinct player-control objects to a caller-owned party;
invalid counts/null/duplicate members leave it unchanged. `bc_runtime_party_frame`
updates the stage once, then each player's controls/weapons once, then one shared
actor loop, and finally each independent option trail. Stage music waits suspend
all player updates and scrolling together. Boss countdown remains one shared
clock. AI's preferred living target rotates every eight scheduler ticks, skipping
dead/waiting members. One-player use delegates to `bc_runtime_frame` unchanged.

For multiple players, checkpoint requests latch individual waiting bits and are
reported once. Other players continue while a member waits. When all members
wait, status 1 hands control back to the owner. The scene owner must debit lives,
reset/respawn the corresponding member and clear its waiting bit, or handle the
whole party's game-over/checkpoint transition. This module does not silently
implement those policies or count a waiting player's death repeatedly.

`qa_bc_party_frame.py` checks 1/2/3/4 independent input/weapon/option-trail updates
against separate player steps, one camera/boss/actor clock, opposite controls,
independent firing, individual/all-player checkpoint latching, stage-audio wait
and acknowledgement, and invalid binding. The existing party collision and
production actor/child-routing tests still pass. The Genesis build and whitespace
checks pass (`.local/pce-reference/party-frame-build.log`). This new frame task
is not yet called by the native scene: multiple-controller rendering, lives,
score/HUD, scaling, menu integration and full-speed verification remain pending.


## Native co-op scene and exact straight-shot packing

The development scene now accepts `dbg_bc_native_players` 2/3/4 (zero/default
retains one player), binds independent controls/weapons, draws the four existing
robot variants, dispatches owner-specific score/audio events and displays a
compact per-player score/lives HUD. Extra score queues use a discarded local RNG
copy, so adding players does not multiply the shared enemy RNG's score-task tick.
Individual checkpoint requests debit only that robot's lives and respawn it in
the shared stage with protection; other players and enemies continue. Exhausted
slots stay out, and all exhausted slots stop the scene with game-over status.
The original solo checkpoint reset path remains unchanged. Round transitions
reset each eligible robot using the source template and preserve individual lives.

Extra controllers initially caused SGDK to fail while unpacking its temporary
boot font. They now allocate at scene entry after that temporary memory is freed,
and release on exit; allocation failure has an explicit debug status $FFFE.
The scene restores the previous player-slot limit on exit. Four-player re-entry
and returning to the menu are verified.

Simultaneous fire exposed hardware sprite-list overflow (121 reported drops in
the initial 4P fixture). Three consecutive identical straight shots spaced eight
pixels apart now render as one 32x16 hardware sprite. Its four tile columns are
composed from the original converted sprite with exact transparent-overlap
priority; horizontal flips reverse the composition order. Collision records,
shot order and motion are untouched. The cache uses separate virtual keys and
256-byte uploads, falling back to individual sprites if necessary. Solo drawing
skips the grouping work. This addresses those observed drops, not general
Genesis sprite/scanline limits or the full-speed requirement.

`qa_bc_party_scene.py --players 2/3/4` drives the actual Genesis core through
independent opposing controls, concurrent fire, a forced death of the last
player, private life debit/respawn and 500 further updates without a repeated
life debit or shared checkpoint reset. Each runs 990 native updates and returns
to the menu with the previous player limit restored. The firing check verifies
actual packed strip VRAM against original ROM pattern pixels/palette. These
fixtures report zero missing art, drops or runtime remaps. Four-player re-entry
also passes. Captures/results live under `.local/bc-party-scene2/`, `3/`, `4/`;
logs are `.local/pce-reference/party-scene*.log`. Build and whitespace checks pass.

The scenes still run below full speed. Encounter density/boss HP scaling is not
implemented in BC yet; these tests use the existing source encounter. This is
not four-player whole-game completion or public-mode integration. Ending
presentation, public mode/modal hookup, physical multi-pad validation and
broader co-op progression/game-over tests remain required.


## Co-op boss health scaling

Boss damage now uses exact rational accounting: 3P consumes two baseline HP
units per three points of incoming damage; 4P consumes four per nine. Composite
bosses and the final serpent head use this scaling; ordinary enemies retain
source HP. One- and two-player contacts keep the original damage path.
`BcActor.health_fraction` occupies existing tail padding (50-byte Genesis actor,
52-byte host actor), resets on template application, and carries fractional
progress across composite health bars. Integral overkill still stops at the
current bar, preserving the source bar transition and protection behavior.
Invulnerable hits do not accumulate fractional damage.

`qa_bc_party_contacts.py` checks exact lethal-hit counts for ordinary enemies,
20-HP serpent heads and two/three-bar composite bosses at every player count.
A 20-HP boss requires 20/20/30/45 unit hits; a three-bar boss requires
30/30/45/68 (the last rounds up from 67.5). It also checks multi-damage hits,
protection, template reuse, owner attribution and the existing single-clock
contact cases. Party routing and frame tests pass. The ROM builds without
warnings and the four-player scene/re-entry test passes at 990 native updates,
2377 emulated frames, zero missing art/drops/remaps, and 17 verified packed
projectile strips. This scene test is a runtime regression check, not a native
exact boss-health-total measurement. Logs: `party-health-build.log` and
`party-health-scene4.log` under `.local/pce-reference/`.

Encounter-density scaling, public menu integration, ending presentation and
sustained full speed remain unfinished. Boss health scaling does not establish
whole-game co-op balance or source equivalence for multiplayer.

## Home menu and player modal

Home now lists Normal, Before Christ and Boss Rush, followed by Options/Back.
All three mode actions open the existing 1/2/3/4-player modal. Before Christ
starts round one with the selected party, normal music acknowledgement and no
debug protection. The dedicated FS_BC value is appended to preserve existing
flow-state values. The native scene owns simulation while this state is active.

A public session resets development overrides at launch. At game over or the
final clear boundary it displays a terminal message and Start returns Home;
A+B+C+Start uses the existing boot-screen reset convention. Cleanup releases
peer controllers and reserved background blocks, restores normal video/game
state, and consumes the exit press before normal menus process input. The final
clear message is temporary: it does not implement the source ending sequence.

`qa_bc_menu.py --players 1|2|3|4` passes real menu navigation, modal cancellation
without settings changes, chosen-party launch, actual audio, terminal return,
re-entry and soft reset. Terminal return is tested by injecting the existing
status boundary, not by playing through every death/round. Captures are under
`.local/bc-menu-{1,2,3,4}p/`; logs are `bc-menu-*p.log` in
`.local/pce-reference/`. The 4P Normal/Boss Rush regression also passes joins,
wave count nine, boss health, settings persistence/migration and merge behavior
(`bc-menu-normal-rush4.log`). The menu logo was moved one row upward to make
space for the fifth item without overlap. The build and whitespace checks pass.

This makes the requested mode/player selection available. It does not complete
BC encounter-density scaling, Home option/continue parity, pause handling,
ending presentation, physical multitap validation, full-game co-op validation,
or the 60 fps / 100% speed target.

## Straight-projectile performance pass

Straight enemy shots now check terrain directly without constructing/copying
homing-flight/resource records. Their probe fields still clear before terrain
checks, terrain death still bypasses common movement/collision and ticks the
lock, and ordinary flight retains the common task. Homing shots continue to use
the original helper; first death updates directly install the same animation,
sprite reference and zero velocity. The simplification remains inside the
existing family dispatcher, with no new actor-loop interface or state layout.

The same round-ten protected solo benchmark (4,000 native updates) improves
from 6,923 to 6,888 emulated frames, with worst sampled work 454 to 452 lines.
The four-player 990-update fixture improves from 2,393 to 2,384 emulated frames;
its 1,303-line maximum includes initialization. It retains zero missing art,
dropped sprites or remaps, 17 verified projectile strips, individual respawn,
menu return and re-entry. This is about half a percent in the solo fixture,
not evidence of full speed or an improvement in every stage. Logs are
`bc-opt-base-{solo,4p}.log` and `bc-opt-inline-{solo,4p}.log` under
`.local/pce-reference/`.

Two extracted projectile-dispatch variants were rejected: an outlined helper
needed 7,295/2,467 frames; a specialized extracted helper needed 7,004/2,433.
Both preserved the recorded actor behavior but were slower on the Genesis CPU.
Their dispatch/header changes were restored before retaining only the inline
straight-shot simplification. Party contact, routing and frame regressions pass;
the finalized ROM builds without warnings and whitespace checks pass.
The retained version also matches 128,454 actor updates in the round-ten source
capture and 109,147 in the round-eight opening capture (5,008 complete loops
each), including immediate/later child updates and retirement. Exact comparison
logs are `bc-opt-inline-source10.log` and `bc-opt-inline-source8.log`.

## Home Before Christ pause/resume

Start from any selected controller now toggles a shared pause. While paused the
scene keeps the last display and a compact `PAUSED - START` label; it returns
before stage loading, input-driven gameplay, random advancement, score/lives,
actor updates, respawns, audio acknowledgement and round-clear delays. Music
already running on the independent sound driver continues. Resume clears the
label and restores the one/two-row party HUD window. Unselected controllers
cannot pause, the existing round-exit pause-inhibit flag prevents new pauses,
and the soft-reset chord works while paused. Launch and teardown clear pause
state. This is Home scene control; the underlying source simulation is unchanged.

The menu verifier now uses linked 68000 symbol sizes to compare complete player,
peer, enemy, stage, score, seed, frame-cursor, defeat, round-exit, audio-request,
scheduler and party records across 60 paused frames of held movement/fire for
every selected controller. It checks resume progress, unselected slots, the
clear-task inhibit, terminal return, re-entry and soft reset while paused.
Screenshots are under `.local/bc-menu-{1,2,3,4}p/paused.png`; logs are
`bc-pause-*p.log` in `.local/pce-reference/`. The physical Start hold test also
checks that holding the button does not repeatedly toggle pause.

Remaining work includes encounter-density scaling, full Home options/continue
integration, source ending presentation, broader whole-game co-op/hardware
validation, and sustained 60 fps / 100% speed. Pause does not address those gates.

## Formation-aware density accounting (not yet scheduled)

Stage-event results now report `wave_size` for successfully allocated ordinary
enemy births: singles, pairs, four-enemy ceiling groups, five-pod formations and
eight-segment chains. Bosses, pickups, controls, audio waits, unsupported events
and failed allocations report zero. This byte uses existing result padding;
source actors, stage advancement and birth effects are unchanged. Tagging the
actual factory paths avoids classifying overlapping handler addresses globally.

`bc_wave_copies` plans total copies with quarter-unit remainders for each group
size. One/two players retain one copy. Four successive successful waves of a
given size produce four/six/nine total copies in 2P/3P/4P, keeping linked
formations intact; 4P's sequence is 2,2,2,3. Different group sizes retain their
own fractional balance. This is counting logic only: it is not connected to
extra actor allocation yet. A scheduler must retain pending copies under pool
pressure, avoid recursively scaling copies, preserve original event order and
handle stage/boss boundaries before gameplay density scaling is complete.

`qa_bc_wave.py` checks 100 interleaved waves of every supported size for every
player count, exact ratios and rejection of non-wave inputs without mutation.
The stage verifier compares all original simulation fields and additionally
checks wave size against immediate birth events, contiguous free slots and
boss/pickup exclusion. Source comparisons pass for round-eight opening and pod
formations, round-ten final boss, round-two ending/curve waves, and round-three
route/middle captures. Successful source wave samples in these captures include
sizes 1,5,8; sizes 2,4 still need successful allocation fixtures. Round-ten's
boss event correctly has zero wave size despite creating eight linked actors.
The verifier's older group-order assertion also now includes the round: address
$B5C5 denotes a single jumper in round two but a chain in round three.

Build, whitespace, party-frame and full public 4P menu/pause checks pass. Logs:
`bc-wave-build.log`, `bc-wave-stage*.log`, `bc-wave-groups*.log`,
`bc-wave-formations.log`, `bc-wave-menu4.log` under `.local/pce-reference/`.
The runtime still uses the original encounter counts. Do not report increased
3P/4P spawning or full speed from this preparatory work.


## Queued co-op wave spawning

Three/four-player frames now enqueue the counted extra copies and replay them
through the production stage factories. A bounded eight-record FIFO stores the
source script address, complete formation size and remaining copies. Copies
are spaced eight simulation updates apart. Replay uses the current camera and
terrain but a copied stage record, so it cannot advance the live stage script,
checkpoint or camera. It runs before player/actor updates, retaining the source
birth-common update followed by the ordinary actor pass. Replay copies do not
earn more copies. Bind/round setup clears the queue and fractional counters.

Failed copy allocations stay at the queue head and retry without consuming RNG
or count credit. Original ordinary births that fail in 3P/4P retain their source
script address and retry too. Stage-event `wave_size` now reports the intended
ordinary formation even on allocation failure (the `slot` result identifies
success), superseding the earlier zero-on-failure metadata contract. One/two
players retain their original stage path and allocation behavior.

When the FIFO is full at a due event, or pending copies precede a boss, cleanup
or scrolling-stop event, camera/event advancement waits. Existing players and
enemies keep running with zero camera delta until room is available. This is
explicit 3P/4P capacity handling, not a 1:1 multiplayer timing claim: dense waves
can lengthen scrolling sections. Original source-event order remains intact;
extra copies use FIFO order. Bosses and pickups are never enqueued.

`qa_bc_wave_queue.py` executes original-code factories for 1/2/4/5/8-actor
formations and checks exact four-wave ratios for all player counts. It covers
full and fragmented pools, retries without RNG consumption, queue wrap/overflow,
FIFO lane order including multiple copies, live-stage isolation and every boss
barrier. This supplies successful pair/ceiling-group allocation fixtures missing
from the preceding metadata pass. `qa_bc_party_frame.py` also checks twelve due
waves overflowing the queue, actor clocks while the camera waits, failed-source
retries, delayed stop events and single consumption of script page markers.

Actual Genesis round-one fixtures reach 800 simulation updates and then stop
new source events to drain the queue. Three players produce 13 originals plus
six extras; four players produce 13 originals plus sixteen extras. Remaining
quarter fractions are retained. Both drain successfully with no missing art,
sprite drops or runtime remaps. These are bounded tests, not whole-game
formation saturation, balance or performance proof. Captures are under
`.local/bc-wave-3p/` and `4p/`; logs are `bc-wave-queue-native3.log` and
`bc-wave-queue-native4.log`. The public 4P menu/pause test, party contact/routing
checks, round-eight/ten source stage comparisons, build and whitespace checks
also pass (`bc-wave-queue-*` logs in `.local/pce-reference/`).

Remaining requirements include source ending presentation, full Home
options/continue integration, physical multitap and whole-game co-op validation,
plus sustained 60 fps / 100% speed. The temporary final-clear message remains.

## Cycle-profiled co-op contact dispatch

`profile_bc_cpu.py` and `bc_profile_hook.c` attribute guest instruction cycles
using the existing hash-pinned Genesis Plus GX core. The diagnostic changes only
its own process's opcode dispatch and restores it in `finally`; ROM/core files
are untouched. `--plain` runs the same fixture without instrumentation, and
`--rom` supports comparison against a saved build and its symbols. The hook is
adapted from the existing local port profiling tool. Results retain the ROM hash.

A protected round-ten 4P sample attributed 23.50% of measured cycles to the
co-op common dispatcher, versus 21.25% in the VBlank wait. The dispatcher used
four temporary event records plus a second pass over every member, even when
all contact gates rejected the actor. Production dispatch now creates a record
only for a possible contact and forwards nonempty events immediately in player
slot order. Motion, protection clocks, early death/bar exits and the caller's
retirement event retain their previous behavior. The array-output common task
remains available as a comparison implementation; no simulation capacity or
spawn counts were reduced. Existing sinks enqueue score/audio and do not mutate
collision state, as required by their contract.

`qa_bc_contact_stream.py` compares both paths in 6,000 deterministic varied
cases, with 1,628 ordered contact events, checking complete actor/player/weapon/
inventory states and counters. Cases cover null/dead/protected members, pickups,
options, terrain retirement, damage locks, fractional boss damage and death.
Party routing, frame/wave queue tests and the public 4P menu/pause test pass.

## Opt-in filtering of empty actor effects

`BcRuntimeEvents` now has an `effects_only` option, enabled by the native scene.
The scene's downstream consumer only queues audio and begins the final ending;
it does not observe every actor update. The option returns early when there
are no extra records, boss-defeat request, setup sound, or parent/child score
and sound effects. Any extra records retain normal processing. Default zero
continues forwarding every completed update, including retirement, pickup and
fire observations, for reference tools and other consumers. The field uses
existing padding between `playing` and the callback; Python reference bindings
and their positional constructors were updated explicitly.

`qa_bc_event_filter.py` compares 5,000 events through the default and opt-in
chains: 2,623 empty deliveries are omitted, with identical score queues, ordered
audio/overflow, ordinary boss-defeat tasks and final-ending requests. Garbage
outside `extra_count` is ignored, event records remain unchanged, and the
default callback still receives all 5,000 updates. The recorded round-ten
reference comparison passes 5,008 loops / 128,454 actor updates / 908 children.
Native final-serpent defeat and 421-update ending handoff pass; presentation

## Home Lives setting in Before Christ

Public Home runs now initialize every selected robot from the shared Lives
setting (1–7 total lives). The source inventory is a reserve counter: zero still
allows the current life and death underflows it to 255. Home therefore starts
with `game_cfg.lives - 1` reserves, while the development/reference entry keeps
its original three reserves. Invalid Home values fall back to three total
lives. Only a new run initializes reserves; individual respawns and round
changes continue preserving the existing debit logic and each player's count.

The HUD has an explicit mode selected before initialization: public Home shows
reserve count plus the current life; reference mode still shows raw reserves.
Underflow displays zero in solo and OUT in co-op. The addition is performed in
the numeric display type, so 127 reserves correctly displays 128 total lives
rather than becoming the OUT sentinel. HUD caching still keys the raw count,
and scene re-entry resets its caches after selecting the display mode.

`qa_bc_home_lives.py` navigates actual Home Options and the player modal. Native
cases cover 1 and 7 lives in 1P/4P, plus 3 lives in 2P/3P. Checks verify configured
reserves, individual debit without charging peers, last-life game over,
retaining decremented counts across a forced round-clear boundary, and refill
only on a new run. Deaths use the existing debug death request; they do not
prove unassisted complete play. `qa_bc_menu.py` now expects the default Home
three total lives to be stored as two reserves; 1P/4P menu/pause tests pass.
The native development 4P scene still starts/re-enters with three reserves and
passes independent inputs, respawn and packed-shot checks.

`qa_bc_hud.py` now covers both HUD rows and both life display modes, including

is visible. Captures are in `.local/bc-home-lives-<lives>-<players>p/`.

## Compact projectile collision index

`BcShotIndex` now stores eligible projectile pixel coordinates as bytes. Its
existing eligibility predicate rejects nonzero coordinate high bytes, so every
cached coordinate is already in 0–255. Target coordinates and collision range
arithmetic retain their full widths. Building the index also advances the shot
record pointer directly while preserving original slot indices and order.
Native `sizeof(BcShotIndex)` is compile-checked at 91 bytes, down from 148:
the four temporary co-op indices require 228 fewer stack bytes.

`qa_bc_shot_index.py` now explicitly checks cached coordinates and min/max bounds
as well as complete weapon/target state and hit events against uncached scans.

including consumed shots, piercing, protection, byte-width range wrapping and
offscreen rejection. Multiplayer routing/restoration and party frame/queue
checks pass. The source round-ten replay still matches 5,008 loops / 128,454
actor updates / 908 children.

## Complete source ending reference

The temporary Genesis GAME CLEAR screen is still not the original ending.
New local captures trace beyond the already verified final-boss handoff:
`round10-ending-presentation` (14,000 frames), `round10-ending-complete`
(24,000 frames), and `round10-ending-return` (23,280 frames, Run at 22,500).
They reuse the recorded forced head-death fixture, so this is an assisted
ending observation, not a natural full-game completion.

The source's $6042 task checks round 9 at $6053 and dispatches $6341, which
loads a separate ending overlay and jumps to $6000. Its CD RAM SHA-256 is
`bbd7f05a8d836aa565e75cabf93a415fa30fc1f47eade5968ed82dfa7ea8788b`.
`pce_oracle.py --late-code-from FRAME` now captures CD RAM and corresponding
bank maps at later snapshot intervals, allowing inspection of loaded overlays
without replacing the initial gameplay dump. These are local reference data;
no PCE artwork or executable code was added to cartridge assets.

The actual sequence is:

1. Congratulations / special completion bonus. $607E reads reserve count $4D
   plus the current robot. $60BC reads remaining continues $4A. The six rates
   at $6293 are 10,000, 20,000, 40,000, 80,000, 160,000 and 320,000, indexed by
   remaining continues 0–5. The ordinary continue path decrements $4A at $64C6.
   $60F3–$610B accumulates three decimal columns; $6112–$6122 adds those columns
   to score, discarding carry above column one. The observed three robots and
   five unused continues award 960,000 at frame 6,973. The visible bonus counts
   upward; total score is redrawn afterward, followed by a three-second wait.
2. Enemy gallery at $9814. Twenty text-record pointers begin at $9D4F. Source
   code scrolls an entry in by eight pixels per update for 32 updates and then
   displays/animates it for 4×64 updates. Observed completed-entry transitions
   are 7,581, 7,870, ... 13,072: all nineteen intervals are exactly 289 frames.
   Gallery portraits in the remaster must use our own corresponding artwork.
3. Staff credits. The text at $AABE uses slash-separated rows and a backslash
   terminator. There are 180 row separators (181 split strings, including the
   final empty string). $9A33–$9A64 advances vertical position by 128/256 pixel
   every two frames, sixteen steps per row. Captured RAM verifies all 2,880

   Captured screens show original CD staff, presentation and license credits.
4. $9A67 waits for controller input, then $9A6F jumps to $3800. With no input
   the completed capture remains at the ending. Run at frame 22,500 changes
   round/playing state to zero; a new overlay appears by 22,560. The 23,280
   screenshot visibly confirms return to the Before Christ title screen.

## Native completion-bonus page

The public Home final-round handoff now displays a completion-bonus page using
our existing Genesis font/palette. It replaces the immediate temporary GAME
CLEAR message for this boundary. Each selected player has its own surviving
robot count, animated bonus and total score; out-of-play players receive zero.
Gameplay actors, players and RNG stop during the page. Start is inhibited while
the bonus counts and for the subsequent 180-update hold. A temporary Home
return remains afterward, pending the gallery/credits renderer. Soft reset and
ordinary game-over return retain their existing behavior. Reference/debug
handoff entry remains unchanged so the source-comparison boundary stays usable.

`bc_score_completion_bonus` implements overlay $60DE–$6122: units of 10,000
based on reserves plus the current robot and 2^unused-continues, three decimal
bonus columns modulo 1,000, addition to score columns 1–3 and discarded overflow.
The helper leaves all other score bytes, queue pointers and bonus-life state
untouched. Invalid continue ranks and out-of-play reserves return zero without
changes. The scene refreshes high scores after applying each award and retains
the old displayed total until the animation completes. Since continues are
not yet implemented, runs currently use the source's five-unused-continues
rate, 320,000 per surviving robot. Continue-policy integration must supply the
rank when that feature is added; this is not an implemented continue system.

`qa_bc_completion_bonus.py` validates 3,072 decimal boundary combinations across
all six source rates and living reserve counts 0–127, unchanged unrelated state,
and invalid/out-of-play inputs. The actual captured 6,972→6,973 RAM transition
matches the native 960,000 award exactly. `qa_bc_completion_scene.py` runs the
native final-round scene with Home presentation enabled and injects only the
already verified clear boundary. Solo checks 96 count updates and a 180-update
hold. 4P uses one, two and four surviving robots plus one out-of-play member,
checking 32/64/128/0 bonus units and independent totals, all intermediate counter
values, 180 hold updates, early Start inhibition, frozen gameplay/RNG and Home
return. Sampling may observe the initial screen upload before its frame returns,
so total frame-counter span includes zero or one initial construction frame;
the count values themselves are checked in order without omissions.

Actual bonus screenshots under `.local/bc-completion-{1,4}p/` were inspected:
all four rows and totals fit, the out player adds zero, and the return prompt is
visible after the hold. The separate final-serpent/handoff verifier and public
4P menu/pause test pass. Build and whitespace checks pass. Logs use
`.local/pce-reference/bc-completion-`. Retained ROM SHA-256:
`d7fd2be8d1f8ef782dbc2949efa72e27cf1bc810bbe2f0b233f7f2ce362e8ce5`.

Final-round protected timing fixtures show 1,644 frames (1P) and 2,046 (4P) for

## Post-ending performance baseline and rejected event alignment

The current credits build's protected round-ten 4P fixture takes 2,096 emulated
frames for 1,000 measured updates after 1,000 warm-up updates, both with and
without instruction instrumentation. This remains substantially below full
speed. The profile attributes 13.74% to party contact dispatch, 10.05% to the
actor loop, 9.73% to scene work, 8.22% to player updates, 6.51% to actor drawing
and 5.10% to enemy motion; 16.17% is VBlank waiting. These are inclusive of only
the named function's instructions, not its callees.

An experimental two-byte alignment on the eight-byte `BcActorEvent` changed
its hot initialization from eight byte clears to two long clears, confirmed
in native disassembly. The 6,000-case streamed/array contact comparison passed,
but the complete 4P fixture worsened from 2,096 to 2,103 frames. It also changed
padding in the containing stage-event result. The alignment change was rejected
and the original header restored; there is no claimed performance gain.

Evidence: `.local/pce-reference/bc-post-ending-profile4.log`,
`bc-event-alignment-{before4,after4,contacts}.log`, and the preserved cartridge
plus symbols in `.local/bc-event-alignment-baseline/`. Next performance work
should target whole dispatch/scan costs rather than assuming a locally cheaper
instruction sequence improves the full compiled loop.

## Cached party contact classification

The multiplayer actor pass now classifies the party while building its existing
shot indices: no living players, all living players protected, or at least one
vulnerable player. `BcParty.contact_policy` occupies the previous padding byte
after the player count. Shot-immune actors skip repeated player scans when the
classification and actor flags prove body contact impossible. Animation,
retirement, cooldown and damage-lock ordering remain unchanged. Player death
invalidates the cache immediately; normal and unsupported exits clear it, so
stage births and player updates never see stale classifications. Event sinks
must preserve player state/protection as documented alongside the preexisting
shot-cache restrictions.

The differential contact check now covers 12,000 cached/uncached cases and
3,232 ordered events. Native-loop routing checks include last-living-player
death followed by a protected actor whose cooldown must remain unchanged,
plus cache cleanup on normal/unsupported exits. Shared-frame, controller,
independent-respawn and scene reentry checks pass. The protected round-ten
timing fixture (1,000 measured updates after 1,000 warm-up updates) changes:
1P 1,708→1,708 frames, 2P 2,001→2,001, 3P 2,023→2,004, 4P 2,096→2,052.
Protection is explicit in this fixture; these are not general unprotected-play
performance claims.

A longer protected 4P round-eight run with bidirectional firing improves from
11,939 to 11,783 frames for the same 4,807 updates. Both runs produce 143 source
and 174 additional enemies, identical remainders and 1,680 queue-blocked updates,
then drain the queue with zero missing artwork, software sprite drops or remaps.
Hardware scanline visibility and full speed are not established by that check.

Logs are `.local/pce-reference/bc-party-policy-*`; baseline cartridge/symbols
are in `.local/bc-party-policy-baseline/`, with independent wave results in

`1267084cb4038ff3ea10e8a0b109bb490806e34390fd52a3cda3c72868dd1ab6`.
The overall ending, Home-option and 60 fps / 100% speed requirements remain

after ordinary/option fire, now runs only when charge handling requested beam
segments. The second check remains after option fire, preserving the source's
case where an option projectile consumes a reserved slot on the release frame.
Projectile movement and slot iteration remain unchanged.

ordinary launches, 198 option launches and 4,088 native collision scans. The
separate 700-frame mixed-pool source fixture passes 4,402 active slot updates,

older fixture replays eight enemy contacts rather than running native collision
scans. Neither comparison alone establishes whole-game behavior.

## Source continue countdown and score reset

New original-game captures `continue-accept` and `continue-timeout` inject the
last-life death and a nonzero score/extend cursor, then either press Run at
frame 3,000 or allow timeout. The first visible countdown state is frame 2,624:
digit nine with ninety updates remaining. Digits advance every ninety updates.
Acceptance checks Run before decrementing the current update, and remaining
continues change five→four at frame 3,000. At frame 3,030 the original clears
the eight score digits and extend cursor, restores two reserve lives, preserves
high score and queue/read/write records, then restores the player at 3,051.
The timeout capture reaches its final update at 3,524 and enters title
initialization, which clears the countdown/remaining-continue RAM in that same
frame. There is no persistent $FF digit in the frame-end snapshot.

`bc_continue_begin` / `bc_continue_tick` implement the ten-digit, 900-update
prompt with explicit waiting/accepted/expired states. Start wins on the last
update; unavailable prompts expire immediately; terminal states are stable.
`bc_score_continue` implements precisely $6501-$650A, leaving high score and
queued records untouched. Disassembly of $6518/$6786 shows that continue loads
the current round's initial checkpoint header before its player/actor reset;
this first-checkpoint capture alone does not prove a late-checkpoint restart.

`qa_bc_continue.py` compares 1,276 source countdown updates across both captures
and the exact 3,029→3,030 score record, plus terminal and final-update boundaries.
Logs: `.local/pce-reference/{continue-accept,continue-timeout}-capture.log`,
`bc-continue-qa.log`, and `bc-continue-build.log`. Build and whitespace checks
pass. The helpers remain unreferenced by the public scene and are linker-removed,
so the cartridge SHA remains the previous `123723923d57c4659a4b41d8dfa284e18b70b526ead1ddc3976b10309df38d93`.
Home continue prompts, limited/unlimited credit ownership, co-op restart policy,
and per-player ending bonus ranks still need integration. The overall goal
remains incomplete.

## Public Home continues and ending bonus ranks

Home Before Christ now offers the source-timed continue prompt independently
to out-of-play members. A new run fills the shared credit balance with Home
credits minus the starting credit, matching Normal's team start. LIMITED spends
one shared credit per accepting player in slot order; UNLIMITED does not spend
credits; OFF or an exhausted balance offers no prompt. Each accepted continue
refills the configured total lives, clears only that player's score and extend
cursor, and preserves their high score. Start is consumed by the prompt rather
than also pausing or returning Home. Expired/out players cannot pause teammates.

While another member is alive, the continued robot rejoins the running stage
with entry protection; shared actors/camera are not restarted. When all members
are out, acceptance calls the current round's initialization with `new_game`
false: the initial checkpoint and actors restart, and only accepting members
are revived. Other members' scores, out status and active prompts survive.
The final round's continue preserves its weapon/power through the source reset,
which differs from the ordinary spare-life death path. Prompts expire after the
verified 900 updates. When everyone remains out after expiry, the existing
Home game-over/Start-return screen is used; the source's complete game-over
animation/fade/title timing is not yet reproduced.

Each member begins with five unused-continue bonus ranks. Acceptance reduces
their rank by one, saturating at zero for Home unlimited/large-credit games.
The completion page displays and awards that player's actual rate, from
320,000 down to 10,000 per surviving robot. A continued player's rate and cursor
persist across round handoffs. Continue processing is gated out of the ordinary
all-alive frame path. Sprites intersecting the top prompt window have priority
lowered for that submission so they cannot cover its text; cached artwork and
subsequent ordinary sprite priority are unchanged.

`qa_bc_continue_scene.py` exercises native 4P limited P4 reentry, independent
score/high/rank records, exhausted credits, unlimited all-out restart through
P2, other members remaining out, timeout without pausing the living member,
and a solo limited restart plus OFF refusal. Injected clear boundaries then
advance the continued player through the real round handoffs and confirm the
160,000 ending rate. This tests restart/continue boundaries, not an unassisted
playthrough. The early screenshot/Start probes were corrected to wait for native
frame completion rather than assuming every emulated frame completes an update.
The initial images exposed sprite occlusion; final P4/team prompt screenshots
under `.local/bc-continue-scene/` were visually inspected after fixing priority.

The public Home Options/4P one-life test now explicitly selects CONTINUE OFF
for its game-over assertions and passes. The complete native 4P ending regression
also passes. Logs use `.local/pce-reference/bc-continue-`; build has no warnings
and whitespace checks pass. Protected 4P timing remains 2,042 frames per 1,000
updates. Retained ROM SHA:
`ce89dd6876640f349a35c6e2325807c12f4c137d22f53f080bbb8520d2e916a0`.

Remaining work includes gallery captions/flash, source presentation and ending
audio, remaining Home options, broader all-mode verification and the unmet
60 fps / 100% gameplay speed target.

### BC common-task call overhead (2026-10-04)

Profiled the retained ROM after the Normal draw change. Protected round-ten
4P attribution reports 11.34% in the actor loop, 10.39% in the party common
handler and another 3.25% in the common entry point. The party handler was
explicitly out of line even though its entry point already provides the
common task call boundary. Inlining that private handler into the common
entry removes that repeated call without changing motion/contact order,
state layout, event ownership, or any collision rules.

### Decode all ending-gallery captions (2026-10-04)

Added tools/inspect_bc_captions.py. The ending uses a custom single-byte
katakana encoding, not Shift-JIS or Unicode. Private inspection of captured
font cells establishes the character map; no source font pixels are packaged
into public/cartridge assets. The tool decodes all twenty captions to Unicode
and records original per-cell codes/positions for later native font rendering.
Examples include ザ ク, ズゴック, ダック, タートル, コマンチ, グローバー,
モヒカン, ファルコンメタル, アトラス, スキュレー, ナイクサード,
ヒートウォーム, センチピード, アパッチ, スレイヤー, ブロンクス,
ジャベリン and セイバー. Entries7/8 begin with an intentional blank row.

Source $9B45-$9BC9 writes ordinary code+0x140 tiles and advances one column.
Slash advances one row and restores the starting column. $BA/$BB marks write
to the preceding column one row above and do not advance the column. The
caption starts at row4, column11 on the entering 32-column page; after entrance
its page column is ((entry+1)*32)&63. Code$75 is spacing; $71 is the meter m.
The decoding composes voiced katakana for readable Unicode while the layout
retains separate mark cells for faithful placement.

Inspection against round10-ending-presentation verifies every complete caption
at a settled entrance boundary, totaling 3,080 exact source VRAM cells across
all20 entries. Output: `.local/bc-caption-review/captions.json`; reference-only
glyph atlas: `.local/bc-caption-review/reference-glyphs.png`. These establish
text and placement, not a completed native caption renderer. Next required
step is independently rendered native font tiles and timed gallery integration,
including scrolling presentation; source font artwork must remain private.
Cartridge code/assets are unchanged this turn. Full-port and 60 fps goals
remain incomplete.

### Six-bit sprite-cache hash (2026-10-04)

Changed the fast-cache index from `(key ^ (key >> 8)) & 511` to a six-bit shift.
All four packed palette bits still contribute to the nine-bit hash. Cache hits
retain exact full-key comparisons, and the original two-way fallback, eviction
stamps, invalidation and upload logic are unchanged. This saves shift cycles
at the cost of a different collision distribution; measurements determine its
net benefit. A five-bit experiment was not retained (it excludes the highest
ordinary palette bit from the index and its short Normal worst case was one
line higher than the chosen variant).

handling in the BC actor loop without forcing expansion in Normal's renderer.

### Conservative whole-party shot bounds (2026-10-04)

The actor pass now caches the union of living players' indexed-shot bounds.
When all living players are protected, an actor outside that conservative
rectangle can skip the ordered player-contact scan. Near actors retain the
existing scan. Common movement/animation still runs first, cooldown and damage
lock still advance once, and consumed shots can only make the cached bounds
wider than necessary. No living player's shot is excluded. The validity flag
is cleared on normal and early actor-pass exit; the shortcut also requires
the cached all-protected classification, which player death invalidates.

The uninstrumented long round-eight 4P fixture improves from 10,866 to 10,717
frames for 5,404 updates. It retains 152 original / 184 extra enemies, 2,253

remains 1,423 frames for 1,000 updates. Vulnerable round-four 4P remains 533
frames for 300 updates. Normal 4P remains 35 misses / worst 304 scanlines over
3,000 frames. The observed gain is in the protected-player workload and does
not establish faster vulnerable play or full-speed gameplay.

Verification: 20,000 streamed/reference contact cases pass, including 798
aggregate-bound cases, 818 empty/protected cases, and 5,112 ordered events.
Actor state/clocks, health fractions, player damage, pickups, options and

### Empty-terrain page cache rejected (2026-10-04)

Tested a data-validated empty-page proof in `BcTerrain`. It sampled every
16x16 subcell in a 256x256 page, cached the immutable cells/attributes pointers,
and returned zero only inside that page with matching pointers. Other pages
and changed table pointers used the original lookup. The host verifier passed
67,108,864 wrapped-coordinate comparisons plus pointer-change/rejection cases.

The first version cached world origin, but round ten actually starts at
(3840,2304), from header bytes $0F/$09. This corrects the earlier inference
that the examined origin page was the initial play area. Both the origin page
and the actual initial page were independently checked against the captured
source map and return zero throughout. Neither fact means the whole map is
empty. The corrected implementation accepted arbitrary page coordinates and
validated the actual camera page at scene initialization.

### Collision coordinate and duplicate-bound experiments (2026-10-04)

Two candidates passed 20,000 cached/uncached 1P–4P contact comparisons but
produced identical frame counts in every measured sample: round-ten solo
1,421; protected round-three 4P 1,659; vulnerable round-four 4P 533; long
round-eight 4P 10,717. Neither is retained.

First, replaced `BcTarget` pixel-coordinate shifts with byte copies from the
middle two bytes of 32-bit coordinates. Generated 68000 code used aligned
stack destinations and individual byte reads, avoiding unaligned word loads,
but the extra stores/loads did not improve measured timing. Second, passed
shot eligibility into `actor_contacts` and let a shared scan skip the already
checked conservative aggregate rectangle. Generic/reference calls still
performed the bounds test and all exact per-shot tests remained intact.
No speed benefit justified the extra parameter and public scan entry point,
so all source/header changes were reverted.

### Alignment-safe common-event clearing (2026-10-04)

Rejected a runtime alignment-guard experiment that used two long clears only
for even event addresses. It preserved all public layouts but slowed 22 BC
openings, leaving 18 unchanged (aggregate +112 frames), solo round ten
1,097 -> 1,105, and long 4P round eight 10,674 -> 10,680. Evidence:
`.local/bc-event-clear-guard/`; rejected ROM
`d7c95e6d0d8f16402c8c93ff5b11bf1365276e420b6ecf705ff026d2e5f2e169`.

The replacement uses two 68000 MOVEP.L writes of zero, at offsets zero and one,
to clear alternating bytes of the eight-byte contact event. MOVEP accepts odd
addresses, so neither a runtime alignment branch nor a structure alignment
change is needed. All public fields, sizes, padding and calling conventions
remain unchanged. Host builds retain the C aggregate clear; a target static
assert prevents compilation if the event size changes. The assembly has a
memory clobber and does not change condition codes.

A separate native 68000 probe executes the instruction pair at all eight
address offsets 0..7, verifying eight zero bytes and all surrounding sentinel
bytes unchanged. The probe uses its own ROM copy, not the measured cartridge.
The 40 opening samples improve 23 cases and leave 17 unchanged, with no
regressions: aggregate 30,196 -> 30,026 frames. Solo round ten improves
1,097 -> 1,085 frames / 1,000 updates. Long round-eight 4P improves
10,674 -> 10,662 frames / 5,404 updates, preserving all spawn/retry counts,
zero drops/remaps and pixel-identical boundary images. Native 4P controls,

### Sprite-cache byte-offset hash (2026-10-04)

Added a 68000 `fast_entry` helper that computes the existing cache bucket's
byte offset directly. Because each target entry is eight bytes,
`((key << 3) ^ (key >> 3)) & 4088` equals
`((key ^ (key >> 6)) & 511) * 8` for every 16-bit key. An exhaustive 65,536-key
comparison verifies this, including unused/sentinel keys. A compile-time
assertion protects the target stride; hosts retain the ordinary typed-array
index. Claim, eviction invalidation, fast hits and slow-path refresh all use
the helper, preserving bucket choice, full-key collision checks, used stamps,
victim order, upload budgets and fallback behavior. Generated code uses two
three-bit shifts instead of six-bit and three-bit shifts.

The 40 BC opening samples improve in 13 cases and remain unchanged in 27,
saving 30 frames with no measurement errors. The long round-eight 4P sample
improves 10,580 -> 10,573 video frames / 5,404 updates, with the same 152 original
and 184 extra enemies, 2,253 blocked allocations, drained queue and zero missing
art/drops/remaps. All 52 actor screenshots and both long-wave screenshots
remain pixel-identical. Normal 4P section nine remains 1,080 frames per 1,000
updates, matching every one of its 1,001 state and sprite-render hashes.
These bounded gains do not establish full speed or complete-campaign fidelity.
Evidence: `.local/sprite-cache-offset/`. Candidate ROM SHA-256:
`7a6e903ed6979d20de16ac63e5f55a8ab69d01c7c49d40ebec66b2c1957175db`.

### Final-boss ordered live-shot list (2026-10-04)

During Normal/Boss Rush final-boss updates only, the first boss collision
query now builds a compact list of active player shots in original player/
slot order. Subsequent parts and projectiles reuse the list, checking each
shot's live state again before testing it. Earlier parts may consume shots
or player deaths may clear them; neither can cause stale entries to hit.
Player weapon tasks run before this update and do not create new player shots
inside it. The list is rebuilt lazily each update and disabled on exit; other
boss kinds and out-of-update queries retain the full-pool path. All four pools
remain included, including hidden partners. Added target storage is 288 bytes
of shot/owner pointers plus three control bytes (subject to linker padding).

across 20,000 resets and 330,128 natural hits, including full-width signed
coordinates, consumed/cleared shots, piercing, debug autohit and retained
initial/last ownership. Added `tools/qa_boss_shot_list.py` compares production
indexed/full-pool paths with the same workload without depending on saved
local source copies. Both checks pass. This does not independently prove
arbitrary external shot births during a boss update; that is explicitly
excluded by the inspected task ordering.

### Native 24-bit actor position addition (2026-10-04)

Added an inline 68000 primitive for moving an actor axis: sign-extend the
16-bit velocity, add it directly to the stored long word, then clear the
unused high byte. On this big-endian target that is exactly the prior
`(position + velocity) & 0xffffff`. The memory operand declares the complete
four-byte read/write and condition-code clobber; host builds retain ordinary
C arithmetic. Existing zero-velocity gates, delays, animation and retirement
order remain unchanged. A size assertion requires the four-byte container.

Added `tools/qa_bc_motion_arithmetic.py`, which extracts the actual primitive
and runs a separate scratch cartridge in the native 68000 core. It compares
655,360 position/velocity combinations against independent C arithmetic,
covering all signed-word velocities, carry/borrow/wrap cases, non-normalized
inputs and both long/word alignment. Volatile neighboring sentinels remain
unchanged. The playable release ROM is never patched by this check. Original
1,594-update common-task replay and 20,000 streamed-contact comparisons pass.

The 40 BC openings improve in 16 cases and remain unchanged in 24, with no
regressions or measurement errors (53 frames saved overall). Solo round ten

10,550 -> 10,544 per 5,404 updates. Spawn/retry counts, drained queue, zero
art/drop/remap faults and both boundary screenshots are unchanged.

### Native stack/peer allocation audit (2026-10-04)

Added `tools/qa_bc_stack.py` and the read-only host hook `bc_stack_hook.c`.
They pin the existing emulator core hash and use its one-argument register
reader (A7=15, PC=16), validating PC against the established core-state offset.
The hook samples A7 before/after native instructions and compares it with the
current dynamic peer allocation's end. Player size is compiled from the target
ABI in a per-run scratch directory. Guest ROM, RAM and CPU speed are unchanged.
The hook is removed on normal/error exit and saves ROM-pinned JSON diagnostics.
This detects stack-pointer overlap with peers, not all forms of heap corruption.

route produces a minimum gap of -168 bytes and correctly fails, agreeing with
the prior observed P4 corruption. The fixed ROM's same route has a positive
1,254-byte minimum gap. Independent instrumented/uninstrumented ending replays
match video-frame count, native tick count and all 64 KiB of ending RAM.

Ran 30 current-ROM charged-fire samples: 2P/3P/4P at each of ten starting rounds,
2,000 updates per sample, with debug protection. No peer-allocation overlap was
observed. Minimum gaps across those routes are 3,282 bytes (2P), 2,258 (3P),
and 1,224 (4P, round eight). Repeated that worst 4P route against an independent
uninstrumented replay: all RAM/frame/tick results match; the instrumented run
sampled 65,366,350 instruction boundaries. These bounded protected routes do
not prove full-campaign memory safety, natural progression or sustained speed.

Evidence: `.local/bc-stack-audit/matrix.json`, `summary.json`, old/current ending

### Read-only VBlank scheduler measurements (2026-10-04)

Extended `tools/profile_bc_budget.py` to observe the compiled scheduler entry,
physical core scanline, pending DMA bytes and VBlank epoch, in addition to the
existing complete-scene timing. The cartridge is unchanged. The SGDK default
`SYS_doVBlankProcess()` selects `ON_VBLANK_START`; `VDP_waitVBlank(true)` waits
for blank to end and then for the next blank when entered during VBlank.

| Protected sample | Scene calls | Mean scene / frame budget | Scheduler entries | Entries in a later VBlank than scene start |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1P round 10 | 1,000 | 75.79% | 999 | 44 |
| 4P round 10 | 1,000 | 104.96% | 1,000 | 463 |
| 4P round 8 | 1,000 | 124.29% | 1,000 | 128 |

Each sample warms up 1,000 simulation updates. A separate uninstrumented replay
matched all 64 KiB of final RAM and the frame/tick counters. Scheduler counts
can differ from scene counts by one because measurement boundaries can fall
between scene return and the subsequent scheduler entry. Read-only entry data
does not establish that a late DMA flush fits the remaining blanking interval.
The 4P round-ten late entries queued 192–1,224 bytes; only 42 of those entries
were in physical lines 224–228. Late submission would require both a VBlank
epoch guard against double updates and a verified DMA deadline. No scheduler
change was shipped on the basis of these observations.

The round-eight scene alone exceeds the full video-frame budget in 942 of
1,000 calls, before outer input/VBlank/DMA work. Scheduler changes alone cannot
satisfy the requirement. Actor loop, actor drawing and common actor processing
are the largest measured round-eight instruction totals; subsequent CPU work
should target those costs while preserving source behavior. Evidence is in
`.local/bc-scheduler-observation/summary.json` and its three per-case results,
including complete scheduler rows and instruction histograms. ROM remains
`c50e582343a017f83e6fc7f8a0a6fb115f13f3612b832170e540ae824ce4ca1b`.

### Sprite-transfer audit and replacement-policy investigation (2026-10-04)

Added optional `--dma-audit` to the Normal fixed-update harness. At scheduler
entry it decodes the SGDK queue's four-longword descriptors, reconstructs
source/destination/step/length, and checks the total against the queue's byte
counter. A temporary host VRAM shadow applies queued writes in order so a
later descriptor sees earlier queued writes. No emulated memory is modified.
Complete 128/512-byte uploads from the ordinary sprite banks are compared with
the destination and inspected cache slots. The other-slot search conservatively
omits two big slots beyond the shared small-sprite region. It does not prove
that no alias exists anywhere in VRAM.

Static bank inspection found 222 duplicate small keys and 17 duplicate big
keys, including many blank images. On retained ROM `8513302e`, Normal 4P
section indices 3 and 8 each ran for 1,000 fixed updates with the audit:

| Section index | Sprite uploads | Sprite bytes | Blank uploads | Identical destination | Nonblank match in inspected other slots |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 898 | 440,576 | 28 | 0 | 0 |
| 8 | 440 | 165,376 | 11 | 0 | 0 |

Both runs match the unaudited baseline's simulation hashes and video-frame
counts exactly. Thus these samples do not justify spending CPU time on a
general pixel-deduplication lookup. Frequent reuploads of big animation images
are the more promising target: section three uploads 66 distinct big images,
with several recurring over thirty times. Evidence is under
`.local/sprite-dma-audit/`, including the aggregate `verified.json`.

### Retained party-wide vulnerable-body rejection (2026-10-04)

The actor pass now caches the union of living, vulnerable player-body centers.
Shot-immune actors outside that union, expanded by their exact byte-wrapped
contact radii, skip the individual body scan. Widened coordinate sums prevent
16-bit overflow. This gate requires cached policy 3: any player death clears
that policy immediately, disabling the shortcut. Protection gained mid-pass
can only make the cached union conservatively wider. The cache is cleared on
bind and at every actor-pass exit. Near actors retain ordered source contacts.
Cooldown and damage-lock decrements are preserved on the rejected path.

The host party bindings follow the added fields. Contact coverage expands to
32,000 cases and 6,917 ordered events, including nonretiring shot-immune actors
at extreme 16-bit positions and hitboxes whose radii wrap to zero. All compare
with the original record-array contact task. Party routing, index/cache cleanup
and complete party-frame checks pass.

### Native eight-byte HUD score comparison (2026-10-04)

repeated work inside the inlined scene HUD. A plain C unrolled comparison was

The retained candidate uses two MOVEP lanes per input on m68k, then compares
their registers. This covers exactly bytes 0..7 and permits odd addresses:

writes no memory. Other platforms retain the existing memcmp behavior.

### Rejected low-memory wheel cell caches — 2026-10-04

Tested three alternatives to the failed 12 KiB wheel-plane allocation: a
1,904-byte per-slot unflipped-cell cache with looped flip handling, the same
cache with unrolled flip cases, and a 3,456-byte complete-cell hash cache.

cache also keyed flip bits. Actual cached/original C routines matched 172,032
cell outputs covering blanks, all flips, regular/extra templates, cache hits,
slot reuse and untouched destination sentinels.

Nevertheless, all three 4P runs retained exactly 2,742 updates / 3,000 video
frames (258 missed). The unrolled version also retained every 1P–3P update
count: 2,805 / 2,541 / 2,788. Its combined frame_cells/cell_words attribution
fell from 172,279,940 to 128,675,876 core ticks, but did not cross the end-to-end
frame threshold. The hash variant saved little CPU and left just 500 free
heap bytes. These results reject CPU-side cell caching as a sufficient fix.
The full-plane DMA/scheduling path needs direct measurement next; reduced
rendering cost alone is not evidence of fewer missed updates.

Restored exact prior source, symbols and ROM `eae08e12e56c15915c60b43c9c2818279f7c32f0e248cc76ff9462265271896c`.

### Wheel-turn CPU versus DMA scheduler trace — 2026-10-04

Extended `qa_boss_rush_perf.py --scheduler-trace` with read-only opcode-boundary
observations at main input, both scheduler entry variants and DMA queue flush.
The 4P 3,000-frame run records 8,226 observations. An independent uninstrumented
replay matches all 64 KiB RAM, final pixels and 2,742 updates / 258 misses.
Production ROM remains `eae08e12e56c15915c60b43c9c2818279f7c32f0e248cc76ff9462265271896c`.

Libretro's video-frame boundary in this fixture is at scanline 224. Duration
analysis therefore uses `(line-224) mod 262` within each observed video frame;
subtracting raw line numbers gives invalid negative work times. The resulting
bounded scanline measurements show 436 ordinary wheel-ready updates at 139–214
lines (mean163.743), versus 246 wheel turns with >=4KiB queued transfers at
377–419 lines (mean395.171) of input-to-scheduler work. Those turns already
exceed the entire 262-line NTSC frame before waiting/flushing. Their flush-to-
next-input interval is 28–29 lines (mean28.008), including scheduler remainder
and input overhead. This does not justify changing VBlank admission thresholds.

The smaller cache's CPU saving was real but insufficient to bring those turn
updates below one frame. The next optimization must eliminate much more of the
synchronous full-rectangle rendering, preserve output, and fit the actual heap.
Evidence: `.local/boss-rush-scheduler/verified.json`. This is a protected route
through three bosses, not all-mode or complete-campaign speed verification.

### Rejected wheel orientation cache — 2026-10-04

Tested storing each slot's last fully oriented cell, keyed by meta and flip,
in the existing 1904-byte cache. Cache hits then use eight native long copies;
misses rebuild with the original cell_words. This allocates no additional RAM.
The uncached-reference comparison passes 40,000 whole planes, including blank
cells, all flips, slot changes, ring wrap and shadow invalidation. The 4P real
Boss Rush route preserves all 3000 complete video-frame hashes. Both builds
free wheel allocations on soft reset.

It is slower: 246 measured wheel turns rise from 306–408 scanlines (mean
327.6504) to 352–420 (mean 373.5122). Both runs still complete 2742 updates in
3000 frames, missing 258. Thus per-slot orientation rebuilding outweighs the
cheaper copies for this route. Rejected; restored bg.c, ROM, ELF and symbols
to `d5a41f8ae089c346f70b89f004dc41de248658628a660a282c34baeb2eedc099`.

Evidence and complete candidate/baseline snapshots:
`.local/wheel-oriented-cache/rejected.json`. Scheduler timing uses physical
scanline epochs with video-frame origin224. End-RAM hashes are not compared
across builds because cache representations differ. No full-game or all-boss
speed claim follows from this bounded protected route. Full speed remains open.

### Wheel shadow-backed copy-plan feasibility — 2026-10-04

The existing shadow plane can serve as part of a complete oriented-cell cache.
Across the five actual wheel maps, only 88–96 unique cells are absent from a
particular current frame. Storing those cells needs 2816–3072 bytes; one
32-byte scratch cell brings the maximum payload to 3104. The measured 4P heap
currently holds 88+1904 bytes of optional wheel caches followed by 1958 free
bytes. Replacing the optional caches appears feasible, subject to native
allocation/lifecycle and stack checks. This is not a claim that three full
planes fit. Raw key counts are conservative (149/149/141/141/154); no assumption
that distinct keys have distinct pixel contents is needed.

A read-only host prototype assigns missing cells to cache slots for each frame
and resolves parallel copies with a scratch cell for dependency cycles. Across
all five maps, 50,000 random transitions (including repeated frames and reverse
transitions) preserve all live shadow/cache cell words. Plans require 112–163
cell copies for nontrivial transitions and 17,408 ROM bytes total, plus small
initial key lists. Unlike the rejected orientation cache, turns need no cell
reconstruction if native residency and invalidation constraints are satisfied.

This changes the next action to a native copy-plan prototype. Initialization
must prepare a valid state without displaying an intermediate frame; slot
reassignment and any ordinary shadow writer must invalidate/recover safely;
allocation failure must retain the current path. CPU cost, DMA deadlines,
render fidelity, lifecycle and actual end-to-end speed remain unverified.
No production source or ROM changed. Reproducible model and results:
`.local/wheel-residency-study/plan.py`, `plans.json`, `feasibility.json`.

### Native wheel copy-plan prototype — 2026-10-04

Added tools/qa_wheel_copy_plan.py. The scratch ROM uses the five actual wheel
maps and deterministic synthetic 16-word cell contents, then checks the whole
shadow plane, all live cache entries and boundary sentinels after every copy
plan. It covers every old/new frame pair, ring wrapping, dependency cycles,
repeated frames, and all four combinations of word alignment for shadow/cache.
Both eight-MOVE.L and MOVEM implementations pass 3600 native transitions each.
The playable release ROM remains unchanged.

Read-only opcode-boundary timing on the pinned stock-speed core measures only
the copy routine plus return/marker overhead, with interrupts masked and no
DMA. Mean scanline costs by wheel0/0h/1/1h/2:
- Eight long moves: 111.50 / 110.07 / 93.89 / 95.79 / 109.61.
- Multi-register moves: 99.31 / 98.18 / 82.42 / 83.94 / 97.62.
MOVEM is the selected prototype for integration. These costs must still be
combined with the real game's other work; they do not prove a 60 fps frame.

The first timing attempt sampled the frame-budget counter before a completed
emulator frame and produced invalid negative spans. Those numbers are excluded
and labeled invalid-initial-timing.json. The corrected probe waits at a native
start gate for one full frame, asserts the 896040-tick NTSC budget and stock
clock scale, then releases the gate under the read-only observer. It asserts
nonnegative intervals and complete transition/alignment coverage.

The native tests prove the copy mechanism on synthetic cell words, not actual
rendered artwork, initialization, allocation, invalidation, DMA deadlines or
end-to-end Boss Rush timing. Those remain the next integration gates. Evidence:
`.local/wheel-residency-study/native-verified.json`, `.local/wheel-copy-native/`
and `.local/wheel-copy-native-movem/`. Full speed and full-game fidelity remain
unfinished.

### Native little-endian actor-data reads (2026-10-04)

The private `word` decoder in `bc_world.c` now uses three 68000 instructions:
load the source high byte, shift it eight bits, then load the low byte. This
supports either byte alignment without changing the two-byte source range.
Early-clobber output and explicit memory operands describe data dependencies;
constant offsets can remain in addressing modes instead of extra LEA operations.
Other modules' address-wrapping decoders are unchanged. The host path retains
ordinary C. `qa_bc_word_read_native.py` extracts the actual decoder into a scratch
cartridge and checks every 16-bit value at both alignments (131072 cases),
unsigned extension, unchanged input bytes and surrounding sentinels.

An initial explicit-address-register version passed the same native probe and
1000 gameplay hashes but regressed late 4P 1746 -> 1755 frames and the long
route 9011 -> 9014. It is archived under `address-candidate/` and not retained.
Inspection showed extra address setup in each template field read. The final
memory-operand version removes that setup and unnecessary saved registers.

### DMA scratch ownership and lifecycle audit — 2026-10-05

The 8192-byte heap allocation is SGDK's temporary DMA data buffer; the 1280-byte
allocation is its DMA operation queue (80 entries), not party storage. It cannot
be lent to wheel frames while queued copies still reference it. Added read-only
flush-time scratch usage to `qa_boss_rush_perf.py` and a reusable driver wrapper
`tools/qa_dma_buffer.py` to observe boot, menus, gameplay and reset. It observes
successful allocation occupancy, not rejected allocations or unvisited paths.
Nested profiler/scheduler hooks are explicitly rejected by the wrapper.

Retained ROM e517ad594b25d920b3ca98d407a505c59e2fb3eee17229178979b23d92214ca1:
4P Boss Rush measured fights peak at 224 bytes, but the complete driver reaches
5760 bytes during boot. The Normal/Boss Rush 4P modal regression also peaks at
5760. The 4P Before Christ menu/pause/reentry/reset regression peaks at **6496**
in Home state 9, with 352 bytes in BC state 14. Both modal drivers pass. Boss
Rush retains 2742 updates/3000 video frames and all 3000 video hashes; the
lifecycle-watched run also matches final RAM. The speed-test exit 1 continues
to indicate missed frames, not an instrumentation error.

Therefore a global reduction even to 6144 bytes is not justified. The starfield
redraw explicitly copies 32 rows of 128 bytes into scratch, although its on-state
source is already persistent ROM. Next evaluate direct persistent-source DMA
for starfield rows (and stable zero rows), then remeasure transition peaks before
changing buffer capacity or introducing compact wheel-frame storage. No game
source or ROM changed in this audit. Results: `.local/wheel-dma-audit/verified.json`
and its lifecycle, normal-modal, bc-modal, and rush subdirectories. Full speed
and full natural-campaign fidelity remain incomplete.

### Native coordinate layout feasibility (2026-10-05)

`tools/qa_bc_coordinate_layout.py` now tests the native 68000 representation
`[integer-high, integer-low, fraction, zero]` against the current
`[zero, integer-high, integer-low, fraction]`. Both retain precisely the same
16.8 position and modular wrap; this is not extra movement precision.
Scratch ROM only, production remains c97f64bda699622ae040d30923856f82129af4926c359773b459590676697ee5.

The original scratch probe mistakenly placed mutable PRNG seed in ROM (.data at
0x3e2504, with no CRT relocation). Corrected to a local seed, verified 96 random
coordinate changes. The corrected probe passes 128,000 paired move/read checks,
plus 262,144 comparisons covering every signed 16-bit velocity at four wrap
boundaries. Guards and low-byte invariants pass. Disassembly confirms direct
word reads in the candidate and the current MOVEP/byte reads in baseline.

Measured kernel ticks for movement with 0/1/2/4 coordinate-pair consumers:
baseline 32816000/55216000/89264000/155568000; aligned
36736000/45696000/57344000/99904000. Movement alone is 11.95% worse because the
velocity must be shifted; movement plus reads is 17.24/35.76/35.78% cheaper in
these kernels. Repeated reads deliberately have memory barriers to model separate
consumers. These percentages are NOT gameplay speed improvements. Evidence:
`.local/bc-coordinate-layout-v3/result.json`, scratch source/ELF and CPU histogram.

Next implementation should start with enemy/actor coordinates and audit every
position mutation, source-byte access, birth copy, scroll delta, culling and
collision consumer. Player/beam structures do not automatically share the same
coordinate width or semantics. Native state comparisons must normalize the
representation, and reference behavior must remain unchanged. Whole-game
conversion, campaign fidelity and sustained 60 fps remain unproven.

### Exact RNG arithmetic simplification retained (2026-10-05)

ROM 03ef47c4e437eb5babd8c201ae917aa84cf6d75db19c3c6056491b44f9a7e859. Source RNG first triples the16-bit seed, then
adds the old low byte into the high byte with discarded carry. This equals
3*seed + (seed<<8) modulo65536. Expressing it directly removes byte extraction
and recombination. Native score entry now saves three registers rather than
four; RNG transition itself uses two adds, one8-bit shift and a final add.

### Word-aligned projectile layout prototype (2026-10-05; not integrated)

Investigated a larger representation change after the incremental instruction work. The isolated native prototype rotates the complete 32-bit projectile position left eight bits: integer pixels become the aligned high word, fraction occupies bits8–15, and the original high padding byte remains in bits0–7. This is invertible even for dirty padding and avoids discarding behavior relevant to source bounds. Production code/ROM remain exactly `c5e38c42c448a0300d03673e72ec464ed13316090f375090168c4de984e991f7`.

Compiled and executed `.local/bc-shot-layout-prototype/probe.py` on the hash-pinned 68000 core. All 1,310,720 cases compare the current production helper, two aligned alternatives and the original arithmetic; every signed velocity at 20 fractional/boundary/padded positions matches final position and offscreen result. Integer-coordinate reads match too. Instruction counters confirm 1,310,720 calls to each of the five measured functions. Evidence: `result.json`, generated C/ELF/ROM, and log in that directory.

The first ADDX version needs a third data register and its saved-register cost makes it slower: 1,322.273 versus 1,252.273 mean attributed core ticks per helper call. A two-register branch version folds the carry into the retained padding byte before clearing it and averages 1,174.838 (about 6.18% lower). Aligned integer reads average 280 versus 476 ticks (41.18% lower). These are noinline callee costs, including their own prologues/returns and excluding caller setup, conversion overhead and game integration. They are not whole-game speed evidence and do not establish that the integrated layout will win. The first prototype and results are preserved separately.

Source audit identifies production consumers in `bc_rules.c`, both projectile render files, and `bc_robot_preview.c`. Packed-triple Y comparison is a critical constraint: its existing `y >> 8` equality includes the old padding byte, so replacing it with only a 16-bit integer getter would alter grouping. The equivalent rotated mask is 0xffff00ff. Births, option low-X masking, index eligibility and all canonical QA readers also need exact transformations. `result.json` records the integration contracts. Native record strides can stay unchanged; canonical readers must inverse-rotate every shot coordinate using each ROM's matching archived header and independently validate that normalization before cross-ROM state comparison.

This prototype makes a larger optimization concrete and testable; it is not yet a production change. Current worst measured production 4P window remains 29.3542 updates/sec. Full natural 4P completion and sustained 60fps / 100% speed remain unfinished.

### Position-only returning-shot prototype (2026-10-05; not integrated)

Inspection found bc_return_step discards both beam_axis boundary results. An isolated helper computes `(stored + ((unsigned int)velocity << 8)) & 0xffffff00` in the rotated layout. This equals the rotated low 24-bit source sum: old source padding cannot affect those low 24 bits, and no boundary carry is needed when its result is unused. `.local/bc-unbounded-beam-prototype/verified.json` and scratch C/ELF/ROM preserve 1,310,720 passing native position comparisons, every signed velocity at 20 full-container edge/padding positions, against original arithmetic and the bounded helper. Initial harness launch lacked the tools import path; adding it allowed the complete native run.

This prototype provides correctness evidence for a targeted returning-shot optimization, not integrated performance evidence. Other weapon families must keep full bounds and X-before-Y retirement. It is the next integration candidate. Worst retained measured window remains 29.5130 updates/sec; full natural 4P completion and sustained 60 FPS / 100% speed remain unfinished.

### Two-register ADDX projectile carry trial (2026-10-05)

validation. New retained R2instruction profile identifies ordinary shot motion
among the repeated player-task costs. In rotated beam storage, shifted velocity

### 2026-10-06 — Shared-engine requirement; prior candidate disposition

The preceding no-contact early-return candidate is retained as a verified baseline, not a 4P performance solution. Production build session 37319 completed and its ROM SHA-256 is `1d3dead522da86c39fc447f20d6cd72db137becfd611bb79ec54008f0d88f505`, exactly matching the tested candidate. The old 4P route adds eight video frames; the expanded route saves eight; their worst 1,000-update windows remain 2,022 and 2,021 frames. Solo saves 54 frames and improves its worst window from 1,400 to 1,394. Normal's 4P matrix remains 10,088 video frames for 10,000 updates (59.48 FPS aggregate; worst sampled section 58.03 FPS). Canonical state, render, Home modal, stack, and Boss Rush checks are recorded in `.local/bc-no-contact-return-native/verified.json`. The 60 FPS goal remains unmet.

The user's architecture correction now takes priority: BC must be a mode of the regular engine, with matching existing graphics reused and genuinely new tiles/enemies remastered. Inspection confirms the current implementation is native but separate: `main.c` intercepts BC before `game_update`/`game_draw`; BC owns separate players, actors, waves, and contact processing. Sharing the low-level sprite/background backend alone does not satisfy this requirement. Further isolated BC microoptimizations are paused in favor of real shared engine integration, while preserving BC behavior with the existing canonical replay oracles.

The latest natural 4P trial's R7 endpoint is a controller-navigation limitation: an independently replayed, input-only 29-update detour reaches the release position, releases the stalled groups, and resumes the script/camera. This proves reachability, not survival or a completed 4P campaign. Evidence remains isolated in `.local/bc-natural4p-first-action-review/`; original recordings are unchanged.
